definition_zh: 地形；地形学；地表起伏与特征的测绘描述
definition_en: the detailed arrangement of surface features in an area, or the science of describing and mapping them
core_image: 测绘员站在山脊上，把周围山脊、谷地与村落逐一标到图上
scene: 测绘员站在山顶，把周围的山脊、谷地和村落位置逐一标在图上： The surveyor mapped the topography of the valley from the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里 topography 指「地表起伏与特征的测绘描述」（第 1 个义项：一个地区地表特征的整体排列）；句意为测绘员从山脊上测绘了山谷的地形。

pos.zh: 地形；地形学（学科义不可数，具体地形描述可数）

forms.label: 复数（指不同地区的地形）

senses.title: The arrangement of surface features
senses.definition: the natural and built features of an area's surface, considered as a whole pattern
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区地表的自然与人工特征，作为整体格局来考虑
senses.example: The surveyor mapped the topography of the valley from the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 测绘员从山脊上测绘了山谷的地形。
senses.why: Topos is 'place' and -graphy is 'writing', so topography is a written portrait of a place's surface.
senses.whyCN: topos 是「地方」，-graphy 是「书写」，因此 topography 是对某地表面的书面画像。

senses.title: The science of describing surfaces
senses.titleCN: 描述与测绘地表特征的学科
senses.definition: the branch of knowledge that measures and represents surface features and elevations
senses.definitionCN: 测量并再现地表特征与高程的知识分支
senses.example: Topography supplies the elevation data used by engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 地形学提供工程师使用的高程数据。
senses.why: The word names both the object and the discipline, because the discipline began as systematic description.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指对象也指学科，因为该学科最初就是系统描述。

senses.title: Relief and elevation difference
senses.definition: the range of heights and slopes within an area
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区内高度与坡度的变化范围
senses.example: The topography rises sharply behind the village.
senses.exampleCN: 村庄背后的地势急剧升高。
senses.why: Relief is the measurable core of topography: how much the surface goes up and down.
senses.whyCN: 起伏是地形可测量的核心：地表上下变化多少。

senses.title: A mapped representation
senses.definition: a map or dataset that shows surface shape and elevation, usually with contours
senses.definitionCN: 用等高线等符号显示地表形状与高程的地图或数据集
senses.example: The topography shows a steep scarp along the fault.
senses.exampleCN: 地形图显示出沿断层的陡坎。
senses.why: By metonymy the word moves from the land to its representation, so a sheet of paper can be 'a topography'.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，这个词从土地转向其再现，因此一张纸也可以被称为「一幅地形图」。

senses.title: Sea-floor topography
senses.definition: the shape of the ocean floor, mapped by sonar and called bathymetry in technical use
senses.definitionCN: 用声呐测绘的海底形状，技术语境中称 bathymetry
senses.example: The topography of the shelf controls how waves break.
senses.exampleCN: 陆架地形控制波浪如何破碎。
senses.why: The same tools that map dry land can map the sea floor, so the word extends downward.
senses.whyCN: 测绘陆地的方法也能测绘海底，因此这个词向下延伸。

senses.title: Micro-topography of a surface
senses.definition: the small-scale roughness or pattern of a surface, measured in micrometres
senses.definitionCN: 以微米计的表面微小粗糙度或图案
senses.example: The coating's topography affects how water drips away.
senses.exampleCN: 涂层表面形貌影响水如何滴落。
senses.why: Scale shrinks, but the logic stays: the arrangement of highs and lows on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 尺度缩小，逻辑不变：表面上高低点的排列。

senses.title: Corneal topography in medicine
senses.definition: a mapped profile of the cornea's curvature used in eye examination
senses.definitionCN: 用于眼科检查的角膜曲率测绘剖面
senses.example: Corneal topography revealed a slight cone shape.
senses.exampleCN: 角膜地形图显示轻微的圆锥形。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the word for any curved surface whose shape must be measured precisely.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词指任何必须精确测量形状的曲面。

senses.title: Abstract: the shape of a field
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：某一领域的格局
senses.definition: the overall configuration of a field of knowledge or activity, including its peaks and gaps
senses.definitionCN: 某一知识或活动领域的整体构形，包括其高峰与空白
senses.example: The book maps the topography of modern poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书描绘了现代诗歌的地形。
senses.why: The metaphor treats ideas as terrain: some regions are crowded, others empty, and the shape guides exploration.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把观念当作地貌：有的区域拥挤，有的空白，而形状指引探索。

intro.en: Topography is Greek for 'place-writing'. The second element is clear; the origin of topos is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: topography 是希腊语「书写地方」。第二个语素清楚，topos 的来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Topos meant 'place, region'. Its deeper origin is unknown; suggested Indo-European links are reconstructions rather than established derivations.
items.cn: topos 意为「地方、区域」。其更深来源不明；所提印欧语关联均属重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Topographia meant a written description of a place, listing its features rather than measuring them.
items.cn: topographia 意为对某地的书面描述，罗列其特征而非测量它们。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek term, and English took it in the sixteenth century for descriptions of particular places.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊术语，英语在 16 世纪借入，用于描述特定地方。

items.en: With accurate instruments, topography shifted from description to measurement of elevation and slope.
items.cn: 随着精密仪器的出现，topography 从描述转向对高程与坡度的测量。

items.en: Sea-floor, micro-surface, and medical uses developed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; exact first dates vary.
items.cn: 海底、微观表面与医学用途在 19、20 世纪发展，确切首见年代各不相同。

note.en: Group one holds place-description words from the same Greek stock; group two holds terms for land shape and mapping.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干的地方描述词；第二组是地表形状与制图术语。

entries.definition: Relating to topography; it modifies maps and surveys rather than naming the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 与地形有关的；它修饰地图与测量，而非命名学科。

entries.definition: A person who measures and describes surface features; the practitioner of topography.
entries.definitionCN: 测量并描述地表特征的人；地形学的从业者。

entries.definition: A place name, from topos plus onyma 'name'; it is a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 地名，由 topos 加 onyma「名字」构成；第二个语素不同。

entries.definition: The arrangement of printed letters, from typos 'impression' rather than topos 'place'.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷字母的排布，来自 typos「印记」而非 topos「地方」。

entries.definition: The physical character of land as something to travel over; topography is its measured description.
entries.definitionCN: 土地作为通行对象的自然特征；topography 是对它的测量描述。

entries.definition: The difference between the highest and lowest points; it is one component of topography.
entries.definitionCN: 最高点与最低点的高差；它是地形的一个组成部分。

entries.definition: The measurement of water depth and sea-floor shape, the marine counterpart of topography.
entries.definitionCN: 水深与海底形状的测量，是地形学的海洋对应词。

entries.definition: The craft of making maps; topography supplies the data that cartography displays.
entries.definitionCN: 制作地图的技艺；地形学提供制图所显示的数据。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real survey terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实测量术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Topos is place; -graphy is writing: topography is place-writing.
normal.cn: topos 是地方，-graphy 是书写：topography 就是书写地方。

normal.en: Do not confuse topography with typography: place versus printed type.
normal.cn: 不要把 topography 与 typography 混淆：一个是地方，一个是印刷字体。

normal.en: The family runs topography, topographic, topographer, topographically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 topography、topographic、topographer、topographically。

normal.en: Contours on a map are the classic picture of topography.
normal.cn: 地图上的等高线是地形的经典图像。

normal.en: Sea-floor topography has its own name: bathymetry.
normal.cn: 海底地形有专门名称：bathymetry。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible landscape drawn only with lines of equal height.
abstract.cn: 想象一片看不见的风景，只用等高线画出来。

abstract.en: Picture a field of study with peaks, valleys, and empty basins.
abstract.cn: 想象一个研究领域，有山峰、谷地与空盆地。

abstract.en: Picture a surface so finely wrinkled that water chooses its own path.
abstract.cn: 想象一个表面皱得极细，水自己选择路径。

examples.en: The surveyor mapped the topography of the valley from the ridge.
examples.cn: 测绘员从山脊上测绘了山谷的地形。

examples.en: Rugged topography keeps the two villages separated in winter.
examples.cn: 崎岖地形使两个村庄在冬季彼此隔绝。

examples.en: Corneal topography is routine before laser eye surgery.
examples.cn: 激光眼科手术前例行检查角膜地形。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「topo（地方）+ graphy（书写）」——把一个地方的高低起伏写下来 → 地形、地形学

root: 希腊语 topographia = topos「地方」+ graphein「书写」+ -ia；经拉丁语 topographia 进入英语。topos 更深来源不确定，所提印欧关联均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from surface arrangement to the science, relief, mapped output, sea floor, micro-surface, medical imaging, and finally to the shape of any field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从地表排列走到学科、起伏、成图、海底、微观表面、医学成像，最后落到任何领域的格局。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surveyor on a ridge marking every hill, valley and village onto one sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：测绘员站在山脊上，把每座山、每条谷、每个村都标到同一张图上。

branches.en: OBJECT AND DISCIPLINE: the arrangement and the science of describing it share one name.
branches.cn: 对象与学科：地表排列与描述它的学科共用一名。

branches.en: RELIEF AND MAP: elevation becomes lines, and the lines become a sheet you can carry.
branches.cn: 起伏与地图：高程变成线条，线条又成为可携带的图纸。

branches.en: DOWNWARD: the same logic maps the sea floor under a different technical name.
branches.cn: 向下延伸：同一逻辑以另一技术名测绘海底。

branches.en: SCALE SHIFT: micrometre roughness and the curve of an eye are both surfaces to be profiled.
branches.cn: 尺度转换：微米级粗糙度与眼球曲面都是待测绘的表面。

branches.en: METAPHOR: knowledge has high ground and basins, and its shape can be mapped.
branches.cn: 比喻：知识有高地与盆地，其形状可以被测绘。

intro.en: Topography is built from two Greek elements and a noun ending, with a full family of derivatives.
intro.cn: topography 由两个希腊语素与一个名词词尾构成，并有一整族派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin topographia is the borrowed form; Greek topos and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 topographia 是借入形式；希腊语 topos 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Topos is the place element in topography.
items.exampleCN: topos 是 topography 中的「地方」语素。

items.example: -Graphy also appears in geography and biography.
items.exampleCN: -graphy 也见于 geography 与 biography。

items.meaningCN: 对某地表面的描述；地形学
items.exampleCN: 地形学记录坡度与高程。

items.example: A topographic map uses contour lines.

items.exampleCN: 地形测量指导道路建设。

items.example: The topographer fixed the height of each peak.
items.exampleCN: 地形测绘者测定了每座山峰的高度。

items.example: The two sites are topographically similar.
items.exampleCN: 两处地点在地形上相似。
地名保存了旧时的地形信息。

items.meaningCN: 水深测量；海底地形测量
items.exampleCN: bathymetry 就是海洋的地形学。

definition_zh: 揭露；启示；惊人发现；真相的揭示；披露；顿悟
definition_en: a fact or truth made known, especially one that was hidden and comes as a surprise
core_image: 一块蒙布从雕像上滑落，原本藏在布下的裂纹与镀金在灯下同时露出来。
scene: 档案馆员掀开盖在旧地图上的布，观众这才看到地图背面还有一整幅手绘的海岸线。 When the cloth was lifted, the hidden coastline on the back of the map came as a revelation.
sceneCN: 这里 revelation 是“被揭开而显露的事实”（第 1 个义项）；句意：布被掀开后，隐藏的图画才显露出来。

pos.zh: 揭露；启示；惊人发现；披露

senses.title: A hidden fact made known
senses.titleCN: 揭露：原本藏着的事实被公开
senses.definition: a surprising fact that has been hidden and is now made known
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏、如今被公开的令人意外的事实
senses.example: The letters contained a revelation about the company's early funding.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件揭露了该公司早期资金来源的一段内情。
senses.why: Revelation comes from revelare, to un-veil; what is revealed was covered, and the noun names both the lifting and the thing uncovered.
senses.whyCN: revelation 出自 revelare“揭开面纱”；被揭示之物原本被盖着，这个名词既指揭开动作，也指揭开后的东西。

senses.title: Truth given from above
senses.titleCN: 启示：被认为来自神明的真理
senses.definition: in religion, a truth disclosed by a divine source rather than discovered by human reason
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中由神圣来源而非人的理性所发现的真理
senses.example: The prophet described his vision as a revelation.
senses.exampleCN: 这位先知把自己的异象描述为一次启示。
senses.why: The veil here is lifted by a power outside the human mind; revelation is knowledge one could not have reasoned to.
senses.whyCN: 这里掀开面纱的是人心之外的力量；启示是人靠推理得不到的知识。

senses.title: The act of unveiling
senses.titleCN: 揭示行为：把遮盖拿掉这一动作
senses.definition: the act of making something known that was previously concealed
senses.definitionCN: 使原本隐蔽之事为人所知的行为
senses.example: The revelation of the documents changed the course of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 文件的披露改变了审判的走向。
senses.why: The noun can name the event rather than the content, so a revelation may be a moment in time as well as a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以命名事件而非内容，因此一次揭露既是一个时间点，也可以是一个事实。

senses.title: A sudden understanding
senses.titleCN: 顿悟：心里忽然亮起来的一刻
senses.definition: a sudden moment of understanding that changes how one sees something
senses.definitionCN: 忽然理解、并改变看法的时刻
senses.example: It came as a revelation that the two problems were the same problem.
senses.exampleCN: 两个问题原来是同一个问题，这让人恍然大悟。
senses.why: What was hidden is inside the person rather than behind a cloth; the veil is ignorance, and it drops all at once.
senses.whyCN: 被藏住的东西在人心里而不是布后；面纱是无知，而它一下子落下。

senses.title: The twist in a story
senses.titleCN: 真相揭示：叙事中揭开的关键信息
senses.definition: the moment in a story when information is disclosed that reinterprets what came before
senses.definitionCN: 故事中披露关键信息、使先前内容被重新理解的时刻
senses.example: The final revelation makes the narrator's earlier silence meaningful.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的真相揭示让叙述者先前的沉默有了意义。
senses.why: A plot works by controlled concealment; revelation is the planned release of what the story was holding back.
senses.whyCN: 情节靠有控制的隐瞒运作；真相揭示就是故事一直扣着的信息被按计划放出。

senses.title: A scandal brought to light
senses.titleCN: 曝光：把丑闻摊到公众面前
senses.definition: the public exposure of wrongdoing that had been kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 把被秘而不宣的不当行为公开曝光
senses.example: The revelations about the factory led to an inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 有关这家工厂的曝光引发了调查。
senses.why: Public revelation adds an audience: the fact was known to some, and the wrong lies in its having been kept from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 公开揭露加上了受众：事实本为一些人所知，过错在于把它瞒住了其他人。

senses.title: Formal disclosure of information
senses.titleCN: 披露：按程序把信息交由有关方面
senses.definition: the formal release of information to a court, regulator, or the public
senses.definitionCN: 按程序把信息交给法院、监管机构或公众
senses.example: The revelation of the financial records was ordered by the court.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令披露这些财务记录。
senses.why: Institutions use the word for the lawful lifting of confidentiality, where timing and scope are prescribed.
senses.whyCN: 机构用这个词指合法解除保密，其时机与范围都有规定。

senses.title: Something that opens the eyes
senses.titleCN: 启示性体验：让人重新看世界的事物
senses.definition: an experience or work that changes one's perception of life or art
senses.definitionCN: 改变人对生活或艺术看法的体验或作品
senses.example: Hearing the cellist play was a revelation to the young composer.
senses.exampleCN: 听那位大提琴家演奏，对年轻作曲家来说是一次启示。
senses.why: The word can praise an encounter rather than report a fact; what is unveiled is a new way of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以赞美一次相遇，而不只是报告一个事实；被揭开的是新的观看方式。

intro.en: Revelation is reveal plus -ation. Reveal comes from Latin revelare, literally to un-veil, from re- as the opposite of, and velare, to cover, from velum, a veil.
intro.cn: revelation 由 reveal 加 -ation 构成。reveal 出自拉丁语 revelare，字面即“揭开面纱”，由表示相反义的 re- 与 velare“遮盖”组成，后者源自 velum“面纱”。

items.en: Velum meant a veil, a sail, or a cloth hung to conceal. The physical cloth is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: velum 意为面纱、帆或用于遮挡的布。这块实物的布是整个词族的基础。

items.en: Velare meant to cover with a veil, and so to hide from view.
items.cn: velare 意为用面纱覆盖，因而指遮住视线。

items.en: Revelare joined re-, here meaning the opposite of the action, with velare: to remove the veil, hence to disclose.
items.cn: revelare 把表示“相反动作”的 re- 与 velare 组合：去掉面纱，因而指揭露。

items.en: Old French reveler carried the sense of disclosing or making manifest, often in religious contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 reveler 带有“披露、使显明”的意思，常用于宗教语境。

items.en: English reveal covers showing what is hidden, whether by a person, a document, or an event.
items.cn: 英语 reveal 涵盖把隐藏之物显示出来，无论施动者是人、文件还是事件。

items.en: The Latin suffix -ationem names the action or its result, so revelation is both the unveiling and the thing unveiled.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -ationem 命名动作或其结果，因此 revelation 既是揭开的动作，也是被揭开之物。

note.en: The first group is the reveal family, separated by word class; the second compares words for disclosure, insight, and sacred truth.
note.cn: 第一组是 reveal 词族，按词类区分；第二组比较表示披露、洞见与神圣真理的词。

entries.definition: to make something hidden visible or known. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 使隐藏之物可见或为人所知；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: serving to reveal something important.
entries.definitionCN: 具有揭示重要内容作用的。

entries.definition: having been made known, as in revealed truth.
entries.definitionCN: 已被揭示的，如“启示的真理”。

entries.definition: the release of information, especially formally or legally. It stresses procedure rather than surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 信息的公开，尤指正式或依法进行；强调程序，而非意外。

entries.definition: a deep and accurate understanding of something. It stresses the mental grasp, not the source.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的深刻准确理解；强调心智把握，而非来源。

entries.definition: a sudden flash of understanding, often with a sense of significance.
entries.definitionCN: 忽然闪现的理解，常带重大意义感。

entries.definition: the act of bringing wrongdoing to public notice, or being subjected to something harmful.
entries.definitionCN: 把不当行为公之于众，或使人遭受有害影响。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: re- plus veil plus -ation. Reveal is literally to un-veil, and the noun adds the result suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：re- 加 veil 再加 -ation。reveal 字面就是“揭开面纱”，名词再加上结果后缀。

normal.en: Re plus veil plus ation: the cloth comes off, and what it hid is now a fact you must deal with.
normal.cn: re 加 veil 加 ation：布被拿掉，布下的东西成了必须面对的事实。

normal.en: A revelation arrives with the sound of a cover being pulled away.
normal.cn: 一次揭露到来时，像一块盖布被拉开的声音。

normal.en: Divine revelation is a veil lifted from the other side.
normal.cn: 神的启示，是从另一侧掀开的面纱。

normal.en: The plot's final revelation makes the first chapter read differently.
normal.cn: 情节最后的真相揭示，让第一章读起来完全不同。

normal.en: A great concert can be a revelation to a young composer.
normal.cn: 一场伟大的音乐会，对年轻作曲家可能是一次启示。

abstract.en: Nothing can be revealed without something having first been concealed.
abstract.cn: 若没有先被隐藏，就谈不上被揭示。

abstract.en: Revelation redistributes knowledge, and knowledge is power, so every unveiling changes a balance.
abstract.cn: 揭露重新分配知识，而知识即权力，因此每次揭开都改变一处平衡。

abstract.en: The most unsettling revelations are the ones that were always in front of us.
abstract.cn: 最令人不安的揭露，往往是那些一直摆在眼前的东西。

examples.en: The diary's revelation that he had known all along changed every earlier judgement.
examples.cn: 日记揭露他其实一直知情，这改变了此前所有的判断。

examples.en: The report's revelations about safety checks forced the plant to close.
examples.cn: 报告对安全检查的揭露迫使工厂关闭。

examples.en: For the students, the microscope was a revelation: the pond water was full of life.
examples.cn: 对学生来说，显微镜是一次启示：池水里满是生命。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（去掉）+ vel（面纱）——把面纱去掉，真相就露出来了。

root: 由 reveal（揭示、显露）加 -ation（名词后缀）构成；reveal 出自拉丁语 revelare“揭开面纱”，由表示相反义的 re- 与 velare“遮盖”组成，后者源自 velum“面纱”，本义为“揭开遮盖后显露出来的事实或动作”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of revelation, all circling one idea: a covering is removed. What was covered may be a fact, a divine truth, a concealed document, one's own ignorance, a plot secret, a scandal, confidential records, or a way of seeing the world.
sensesIntro.cn: revelation 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：遮盖被取下。被盖住的可以是事实、神圣真理、被隐藏的文件、自己的无知、情节秘密、丑闻、机密记录，或一种看世界的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth sliding off a statue, cracks and gilding appearing together under the lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布从雕像上滑落，裂纹与镀金在灯下同时露出来。

chain: REVELATION THE UNVEILING AND WHAT IS UNVEILED

branches.en: THE FACT AND THE ACT: a hidden truth made public, and the moment of making it public.
branches.cn: 事实与动作：被公开的隐藏真相，以及公开它的那个时刻。

branches.en: THE VEIL LIFTED FROM ABOVE: truth received rather than reasoned out.
branches.cn: 面纱由上方掀开：被接受而非被推理得出的真理。

branches.en: THE VEIL INSIDE: an inner ignorance that suddenly drops, and an encounter that changes perception.
branches.cn: 内侧的面纱：忽然落下的内在无知，以及改变感知的一次相遇。

branches.en: THE PLANNED RELEASE: a story's withheld information delivered at the chosen moment.
branches.cn: 有计划的释放：故事扣住的信息在选定时刻交付。

branches.en: PUBLIC AND FORMAL EXPOSURE: a scandal brought into the open and records released under order.
branches.cn: 公开与正式披露：丑闻被摊开，记录依命令交出。

intro.en: Revelation is reveal plus -ation. The family includes revelatory and unrevealed, with -atory marking what serves to reveal and un- marking what stays hidden.
intro.cn: revelation 由 reveal 加 -ation 构成。词族包括 revelatory 与 unrevealed，其中 -atory 标记有助于揭示之物，un- 标记仍被隐藏者。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layers are velum, velare, and revelare. The prefix re- here does not mean again but the undoing of the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层次是 velum、velare 与 revelare。这里的前缀 re- 不表示“再一次”，而表示动作的撤销。

items.example: The Latin word also gives English veil and velum in anatomy.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词也给出英语 veil（面纱）以及解剖学中的 velum（软腭）。

items.example: The verb described covering a statue before a festival.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词可描述节庆前把雕像遮起来。

items.example: The scan revealed a crack beneath the paint.
items.exampleCN: 扫描显示颜料下面有一道裂缝。

items.meaning: the unveiling, or the thing unveiled
items.example: The letters were a revelation to the biographer.
items.exampleCN: 这些信件对传记作者来说是一个重大发现。

items.example: The interview was revelatory about his early years.
items.exampleCN: 这次访谈对他早年的经历很有揭示性。

items.example: Revealed preferences differ from what people say they want.
items.exampleCN: 显示出来的偏好与人们口头上说的并不相同。

items.example: The cause of the fire remains unrevealed.
The minutes are revealing about how the vote was arranged.
items.exampleCN: 会议记录透露了投票是如何安排的。

items.meaning: a cloth worn or hung to conceal
items.example: She lifted her veil at the altar.

definition_zh: vt. 危及；使遭到危险；危害
definition_en: to put someone or something in a situation where harm or loss is possible
core_image: 堤坝上出现一道细缝，巡坝人把标记旗插下去，下游村庄的灯还亮着
scene: 巡坝人在细缝旁插下标记旗，下游村庄的灯还亮着。 The crack could endanger the village downstream.
sceneCN: 这里 endanger 指「危及」（第 1 个义项：使某人或某物处于可能受害的境地）；句意是这道裂缝可能危及下游的村庄。

pos.zh: 危及；使遭到危险；危害

senses.title: To put at risk
senses.definition: to put someone or something in a situation where harm is possible
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使某人或某物处于可能受害的境地
senses.example: The crack could endanger the village downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 这道裂缝可能危及下游的村庄。
senses.why: A marker flag pushed into a thin crack while the lights of a village still burn below
senses.whyCN: 标记旗插进一道细缝，下游村庄的灯还亮着

senses.title: To threaten a species
senses.definition: to bring a species close to dying out
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使一个物种接近灭绝
senses.example: Draining the marsh would endanger the birds that nest there.
senses.exampleCN: 排干沼泽会危及在那里筑巢的鸟类。
senses.why: A nest count that falls from forty pairs to four in ten years
senses.whyCN: 巢数十年间从四十对降到四对

senses.title: To expose to serious risk
senses.definition: to expose a plan or a person to serious loss or blame
senses.definitionCN: （动词）使计划或个人面临重大损失或责难
senses.example: Publishing the names would endanger the witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 公布这些姓名会危及证人。
senses.why: A list of names left on a desk beside an open window
senses.whyCN: 一份名单留在靠窗敞开的桌上

intro.en: Endanger is en- plus danger, from Old French dangier, power or lordship, from Latin dominium; to endanger is to put a thing under a power that can harm it.
intro.cn: endanger 由 en- 加 danger 组成，danger 来自古法语 dangier（权力、支配），源自拉丁语 dominium；endanger 就是把东西置于一种能伤害它的力量之下。

items.en: Dominium means ownership or lordship, from dominus, a master.
items.cn: dominium 意为所有权、支配权，来自 dominus（主人）。

items.en: Dangier means power to harm or the reach of a lord.
items.cn: dangier 意为伤害的权力、领主势力所及。

items.en: English danger first means power or jurisdiction, then peril.
items.cn: 英语 danger 最初指权力、管辖，后指危险。

items.en: English forms endanger from en- plus danger, to put in peril.
items.cn: 英语由 en- 加 danger 造出 endanger，意为置于危险中。

items.en: The participle endangered is used of species at risk of dying out.
items.cn: 分词 endangered 用于指有灭绝风险的物种。

items.en: Law uses endangerment for conduct that creates a risk of harm.
items.cn: 法律用 endangerment 指造成损害风险的行为。

note.en: Endanger, danger and dangerous share Old French dangier, power to harm; threaten and jeopardize are near in meaning but carry no idea of lordship.
note.cn: endanger、danger 与 dangerous 共享古法语 dangier（伤害的权力）；threaten 与 jeopardize 意思接近，却不带支配权的意味。

dict_mnemonic.text: endanger ＝ en-（使进入）＋ danger（危险，古法语 dangier「支配权」，拉丁 dominium）＝「使进入危险之中」。名词 danger 危险，形容词 dangerous 危险的，名词 endangerment 危及、危害，副词 dangerously 危险地。三类用法：安全 endanger lives 危及生命、endanger health 危害健康、endanger the public 危及公众；物种 endanger the species 危及物种，分词 endangered species 濒危物种；风险 endanger national security 危及国家安全、endanger the witnesses 危及证人。注意 endanger 是及物动词，直接接宾语，不加 to；dangerous 才是形容词。词源上 danger 原指领主的支配权，落在谁手里谁就危险。

root: en-（使进入）＋ 拉丁语 dominium（支配权）→ 古法语 dangier → danger（危险）→ endanger（使陷入危险）

definition_zh: 大灾难；毁灭性结局；悲剧的收场；彻底失败
definition_en: a sudden, widespread and ruinous event, or the disastrous end of a process
core_image: 舞台上的幕布在一个转身之间砸落，台上所有布景一次全毁
scene: 地震后的港口只剩扭曲的吊车与倾覆的货轮，经济学家称这场连锁崩塌为大灾难。 The harbour after the earthquake held only twisted cranes and a capsized freighter, a catastrophe that economists traced through every linked industry.
sceneCN: 这里 catastrophe 指「范围广、破坏彻底且带有终结意味的灾难」（第 1 个义项：造成全面毁灭的重大灾变）；句意为地震后的港口只剩扭曲吊车与倾覆货轮，经济学家称这场连锁崩塌为大灾难。可辨识物件：扭曲吊车、倾覆船体、断裂栈桥、漂浮货柜。

pos.zh: 大灾难；毁灭性结局（可数）

forms.label: 相关形容词（戏剧结局的）

derivatives.zh: 把小事想成灾难；灾难化

senses.title: A ruinous event on a wide scale
senses.titleCN: 范围广泛的毁灭性事件
senses.definition: a sudden event that destroys lives, property or systems on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生、大规模摧毁生命、财产或体系的事件
senses.example: The dam failure was a catastrophe for four downstream towns.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝失事对下游四个城镇是一场大灾难。
senses.why: the Greek original meant an overturning, so the word's core is a whole order turned over at once.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原义是「翻转」，因此这个词的核心是一整套秩序被一次掀翻。

senses.title: The final ruin of a drama
senses.definition: the closing turn of a tragedy in which the hero's fortune is destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 悲剧的收场转折，主人公的命运在此被彻底毁掉
senses.example: In the last scene the catastrophe arrives not as death but as recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一幕，灾难性的收场不是死亡，而是认出真相。
senses.why: Aristotle used the word for the final change of fortune, and English drama criticism kept that technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 亚里士多德用这个词指命运的最终转变，英语戏剧评论保留了这个专门义。

senses.title: A total failure of a plan
senses.titleCN: 计划或尝试的彻底失败
senses.definition: an attempt or arrangement that ends in complete failure
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底失败告终的尝试或安排
senses.example: The launch was a catastrophe: the rocket never left the pad.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发射是一场彻底的失败：火箭根本没离开发射台。
senses.why: the ruin is no longer physical; what is overturned is the expectation built around the plan.
senses.whyCN: 毁灭不再是物理上的，被掀翻的是围绕计划建立起来的期待。

senses.title: A sudden change in a system
senses.definition: an abrupt, discontinuous change in a mathematical or physical system
senses.definitionCN: 数学或物理系统中突然、不连续的变化
senses.example: Catastrophe theory models how a bridge's curve jumps from one shape to another.
senses.exampleCN: 突变理论研究桥面曲线如何从一个形状跳到另一个。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the overturning image for a fold in a surface where a small push causes a large jump.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用了「翻转」意象，指曲面上某一折处：轻推一下，结果却大幅跳变。

senses.title: An ecological collapse
senses.definition: the collapse of an ecosystem past a threshold from which it cannot return
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统越过阈值、无法回到原状的崩溃
senses.example: Once the reef bleached, the fishery slid toward catastrophe.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁一旦白化，渔业便滑向崩溃。
senses.why: ecologists use the word for a threshold crossing because the old state really is overturned, not merely damaged.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家用它指越过阈值，因为旧状态是真的被掀翻了，而不只是受损。

senses.title: A humanitarian emergency
senses.definition: a crisis in which a large population loses shelter, food or medical care at once
senses.definitionCN: 大量人口同时失去住所、食物或医疗的危机
senses.example: Aid agencies warned of a humanitarian catastrophe if the border stayed closed.
senses.exampleCN: 援助机构警告，若边界持续关闭，将出现人道主义灾难。
senses.why: the word scales the harm to a population, which is why agencies pair it with humanitarian.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把损害放大到一个群体，因此机构常把它与人道主义一词搭配。

senses.title: The catastrophic ending of a story
senses.titleCN: 故事或局势的灾难性结局
senses.definition: the irreversible disastrous outcome toward which a story or situation is moving
senses.definitionCN: 故事或局势正走向的、不可逆的灾难性结局
senses.example: Every negotiation that ignored the debt was heading for the same catastrophe.
senses.exampleCN: 每一场无视债务的谈判都走向同一个灾难结局。
senses.why: the dramatic sense spread to ordinary narrative: a plot's final overturning can be economic or political.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧义扩展到日常叙事：情节的最终翻转可以是经济的，也可以是政治的。

senses.title: Abstract: any overwhelming ruin
senses.definition: a metaphorical label for any overwhelming ruin that feels final and total
senses.definitionCN: 隐喻标签，指任何显得彻底且终结性的压倒性毁灭
senses.example: The review called the film a catastrophe, and the box office agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 评论把这部电影称为一场灾难，票房也印证了这一点。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the core of total overturning, dropping every physical detail.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻只保留「彻底翻转」这一核心，丢掉了所有物理细节。

intro.en: Catastrophe comes from Greek katastrophē 'an overturning', built on kata- 'down' and strephein 'to turn'. It entered English through Latin and French, first as a term of drama. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: catastrophe 来自希腊 katastrophē「翻转」，由 kata-「向下」与 strephein「转」构成。它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初是戏剧术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Strephein meant 'to turn, twist'; its further origin is not established, so any reconstructed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: strephein 意为「转、扭」；其更远来源未得到证明，任何重构词根都只是假说。

items.en: Kata- 'down' plus strephein gave katastrophē, 'an overturning, a sudden end', used of a turning point in a play.
items.cn: kata-「向下」加 strephein 构成 katastrophē「翻转、突然的终结」，用于指戏剧中的转折。

items.en: Latin took the word as catastrophа, keeping the dramatic sense of a final reversal of fortune.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 catastrophа，保留了「命运最终逆转」的戏剧义。

items.en: French catastrophe reached English in the sixteenth century as a stage term, then widened to any great disaster by the eighteenth.
items.cn: 法语 catastrophe 于 16 世纪进入英语，先作舞台术语，到 18 世纪扩展到泛指一切大灾难。

items.en: Geology used catastrophe for sudden global change in the debate over catastrophism, and mathematics later named catastrophe theory after the same image.
items.cn: 地质学在灾变论之争中用 catastrophe 指突然的全球变化，数学后来的突变理论也沿用同一意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of strephein is unsettled, and the exact date when the general 'disaster' sense displaced the stage sense is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：strephein 在希腊语之前的历史未定，泛指「灾难」的义项取代舞台义的确切年代亦不可考。

note.en: Group one holds ruin words that differ in reach and cause; group two holds words for the human response or the study of such events.
note.cn: 第一组是范围与成因不同的毁灭类词；第二组指人的应对反应或对此类事件的研究。

entries.definition: From Greek astron through 'ill star': a disaster may be local, and its cause may be human or natural, so it is wider in origin but often smaller in scale.
entries.definitionCN: 经「凶星」来自希腊 astron：disaster 可大可小，成因可人为可自然，因此来源更宽而规模常更小。

entries.definition: From Latin calamitas 'loss, damage': it stresses the distress people feel rather than a whole order overturned.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 calamitas「损失、损害」：强调人们承受的苦难，而非整套秩序的翻转。

entries.definition: Greek kataklysmos 'a deluge': it stresses an overwhelming physical rush, especially water or upheaval.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊 kataklysmos「洪水」：强调压倒性的物理冲击，尤其是水或地壳剧变。

entries.definition: From French débâcle, a breaking up of ice in a river: a spectacular collapse or rout, usually of a plan or an army.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 débâcle「河中冰层崩解」：指壮观的崩溃或溃败，多用于计划或军队。

entries.definition: A serious drama with a sorrowful end; as a general noun it stresses grief and pity, while catastrophe stresses the ruin itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以悲伤结局收场的严肃戏剧；作一般名词时强调悲痛与怜悯，而 catastrophe 强调毁灭本身。

entries.definition: From Greek krisis 'decision': the decisive moment that may end well or badly, so it precedes the catastrophe rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 krisis「决断」：可能好也可能坏的决胜时刻，因此在灾难之前，而不是灾难本身。

entries.definition: A sudden situation calling for immediate action; it names the period of response, not the scale of the ruin.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要立即行动的突发状况；它指响应时段，而非毁灭的规模。

entries.definition: The geological view that Earth's history was shaped by sudden global upheavals; it is a doctrine about catastrophes, not one itself.
entries.definitionCN: 地质学观点，认为地球历史由突然的全球剧变塑造；它是关于灾变的学说，本身不是灾变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: kata- means down and strephein means turn, so catastrophe is a turning down, an overturning.
normal.cn: kata- 表示「向下」，strephein 表示「转」，catastrophe 就是「向下翻转」，即倾覆。

normal.en: The stage sense came first: the catastrophe is the final reversal of a tragedy.
normal.cn: 舞台义最先出现：catastrophe 是悲剧中命运的最终逆转。

normal.en: The adjective is catastrophic, as in catastrophic flooding or a catastrophic failure.
normal.cn: 形容词是 catastrophic，如灾难性洪水或灾难性故障。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: environmental catastrophe, humanitarian catastrophe.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：环境大灾难、人道主义灾难。

normal.en: Geology and mathematics keep technical uses: catastrophism and catastrophe theory.
normal.cn: 地质学与数学保留专业用法：灾变论与突变理论。

abstract.en: Picture a stage curtain falling in the middle of the play and taking the set with it.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布在戏演到一半时落下，把布景一起带倒。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of ice on a river breaking all at once with a sound like a shot.
abstract.cn: 想象河面冰层轰然一次崩裂，响声如同枪响。

abstract.en: Picture a folded map where one crease, once pressed, flips the whole sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折过的地图，按下其中一道折痕，整张纸便翻面。

examples.en: The failure of the levee was a catastrophe that reshaped the city for a generation.
examples.cn: 堤坝失事是一场大灾难，重塑了这座城市整整一代人。

examples.en: Ignoring the early warnings turned a manageable flood into a catastrophe.
examples.cn: 无视早期预警，把一场可控的洪水变成了大灾难。

examples.en: In the final act the catastrophe is a recognition, not a death.
examples.cn: 在最后一幕，悲剧的收场是一次认出，而非一死。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cat（猫）+ astro（星）+ phe」——猫盯着灾星，一次翻身全毁 → 大灾难

root: 希腊 katastrophē「翻转」= kata-「向下」+ strephein「转」，经拉丁 catastrophа 与法语进入英语；strephein 的更深来源不确定。英语 catastrophe。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one overturning: first a whole order destroyed, then the stage reversal, then any plan or system that flips, and finally the metaphor for total ruin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「翻转」展开：先是整套秩序被毁，再是舞台上的逆转，接着是计划或系统的翻转，最后是对彻底毁灭的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole set is overturned in a single movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：整套布景在一次动作中被掀翻。

branches.en: SCALE OF HARM: the overturning is measured by how many lives and systems go down with it.
branches.cn: 损害规模：翻转的轻重，取决于多少生命与体系随之倒下。

branches.en: DRAMATIC ARC: the stage reversal and the story's ending share one final turn.
branches.cn: 戏剧弧线：舞台逆转与故事结局共用同一次最终转折。

branches.en: PLAN FAILURE: nothing physical breaks, but the expectation is overturned.
branches.cn: 计划失败：没有实物破碎，被掀翻的是期待。

branches.en: SYSTEM THRESHOLD: mathematics and ecology both describe a small push that flips a state.
branches.cn: 系统阈值：数学与生态学都描述「轻推一下、状态翻面」。

branches.en: METAPHOR: only the claim of total finality survives when the word is used loosely.
branches.cn: 隐喻：宽泛使用这个词时，只剩「彻底且终结」这一主张。

intro.en: Catastrophe is a Greek compound whose two parts also build a small family of English technical words, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: catastrophe 是一个希腊复合词，两部分还构成一小族英语技术词，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: The Greek prefix kata- appears in cataclysm and catalog; the root strephein appears in strophe and in the technical adjective catastrophic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊前缀 kata- 出现在 cataclysm 与 catalog 中；词根 strephein 出现在 strophe 与形容词 catastrophic 中。

items.example: The prefix turns the movement downward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作转向下方。
那场洪水是一场大灾难。

items.meaning: a turning away to address someone
items.example: The poem opens with an apostrophe to the night.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗以对夜的呼告开篇。

items.meaning: the doctrine of sudden global change
items.exampleCN: 灾变论曾与均变论相抗衡。

items.meaning: to treat a small trouble as ruin
items.example: She tends to catastrophize a single mistake.
items.exampleCN: 她容易把一次错误想成灾难。

latinEntries.structure: catastrophа, catastrophae (f., first declension, Latinized Greek)
latinEntries.meaning: an overturning; the final turn of a play
a turn, a stanza sung while turning

definition_zh: 引出；诱出；引起（反应）
definition_en: to draw out a response, fact or feeling that was not offered freely
core_image: 一根细线从水面下慢慢提起，把藏在深处的东西一点点带出水面
scene: 记者把录音笔推到桌子中间，只问了一个很轻的问题。 The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
sceneCN: 这里 elicit 指引出回答或信息（第 1 个义项：把未主动说出的东西带出来）；句意为这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。

pos.zh: 引出；诱出；引起

senses.title: Draw out an answer
senses.definition: to get someone to say something they had not planned to say
senses.definitionCN: 使某人说出原本没打算说的话
senses.example: The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。
senses.why: The word assumes resistance: the answer exists but is not on the surface, so it must be drawn.
senses.whyCN: 这个词预设了阻力：答案存在，却不在表面，因此必须被拉出来。

senses.title: Obtain a reaction
senses.definition: to produce a response from a body, a market or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 使身体、市场或人群产生反应
senses.example: The new rule elicited protests from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定引起每个部门的抗议。
senses.why: Reactions are also hidden until something touches them, and the touch is what elicits.
senses.whyCN: 反应也一直藏着，直到有东西触碰；而触碰就是 elicit。

senses.title: Extract a confession
senses.definition: to draw out an admission through questioning rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 通过提问而非强力取得承认
senses.example: The lawyer elicited a detail the witness had forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 律师引出了证人已经忘记的一个细节。
senses.why: Careful questioning works like fishing: it does not push, it waits and lifts.
senses.whyCN: 细致的问话像钓鱼：不推，只等，然后提起来。

senses.title: Evoke a memory
senses.definition: to bring a half-lost memory back into speech or mind
senses.definitionCN: 把半失的记忆带回言语或意识中
senses.example: The old song elicited a story about his first job.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌唤起了一个关于他第一份工作的故事。
senses.why: Memory is stored below speech; a small cue can pull it up whole.
senses.whyCN: 记忆储存在言语之下；一个小小的线索就能把整块提上来。

senses.title: Win applause
senses.definition: to cause an audience to give a visible sign of approval
senses.definitionCN: 使观众给出可见的赞许表示
senses.example: Her final line elicited applause that lasted a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她最后一句赢得了持续一分钟的掌声。
senses.why: Applause is offered, not commanded, so when it is elicited the performance has done the pulling.
senses.whyCN: 掌声是自愿给出的，不是被命令的，因此被引出时，是表演做了拉动。

senses.title: Gather information
senses.definition: to obtain facts from people or systems by skilled asking
senses.definitionCN: 通过有技巧的询问从人或系统中取得事实
senses.example: The survey elicited useful answers about commuting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查获取了关于通勤的有用回答。
senses.why: In research the word is neutral: information is collected by design, not by luck.
senses.whyCN: 在研究语境中这个词是中性的：信息按设计收集，而非靠运气。

senses.title: Draw out a smile
senses.definition: to cause a small, often involuntary expression of pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 使一个细小、常常不由自主的愉快表情出现
senses.example: A single silly drawing elicited a smile from the child.
senses.exampleCN: 一幅傻气的简笔画逗出了孩子的微笑。
senses.why: A smile is the least guarded reaction, which makes it the clearest proof of eliciting.
senses.whyCN: 微笑是最不设防的反应，因此是「引出」最清楚的证据。

senses.title: Provoke a response
senses.definition: to stir a strong response, sometimes against the responder's will
senses.definitionCN: 激起强烈回应，有时违背回应者的意愿
senses.example: The speech elicited anger he had not expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这场演讲激起了他未曾预料的愤怒。
senses.why: Here eliciting shades toward provoking: the response comes out before it can be filtered.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 elicit 已偏向 provoke：回应还没来得及过滤就出来了。

intro.en: Elicit comes from a Latin verb meaning to lure out, and its old cousins include lace and delicacy.
intro.cn: elicit 来自一个意为「诱出」的拉丁动词，它的古老亲属包括 lace 与 delicacy。

items.en: English took the verb in the 17c. from Latin, mostly in scholarly prose.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，多见于学术文字。

items.en: Elicere meant 'to draw out, to entice forth', as bait draws a fish.
items.cn: elicere 意为「引出、诱出」，像饵把鱼引出来。

items.en: The prefix ex- means out; the motion is always from inside to surface.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 意为向外；动作总是从内部到表面。

items.en: Lacere 'to entice' is the base, related to the idea of a lure.
items.cn: lacere「引诱」是词基，与「饵」的观念相关。

items.en: Modern English uses it for answers, data and reactions, all drawn out by method.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指回答、数据与反应，都是被方法引出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds nearly identical and is often confused; the near-meaning group names other ways of bringing something forth.
note.cn: 形近组读音几乎相同，常被混淆；近义组列出其它把事物带出来的方式。

entries.definition: forbidden by law or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 被法律或规则禁止的。

entries.definition: the act of drawing something out.
entries.definitionCN: 引出某物的行为。

entries.definition: a person or thing that draws out a response
entries.definitionCN: 诱出者；引出物

entries.definition: omitted or merged in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 被省略或读音合并的。

entries.definition: to bring a memory or feeling into the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把记忆或情感唤入心中。

entries.definition: to remove something by force or process.
entries.definitionCN: 用力量或工序取出某物。

entries.definition: to stir a strong response, often deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 激起强烈回应，常为有意。

entries.definition: to bring out something that exists in hidden form.
entries.definitionCN: 把以隐藏形式存在的东西带出来。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a line lifting something slowly from under the water.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一根线把水下的东西慢慢提上来」的画面。

normal.en: Elicit begins like e-lect: a question elects one answer out of many.
normal.cn: elicit 开头像 e-lect：一个问题从许多答案中选出一个。

normal.en: Elicit and illicit differ by one letter and a whole moral world.
normal.cn: elicit 与 illicit 只差一个字母，却隔着一整个道德世界。

normal.en: Think of a fisherman waiting, not pulling hard.
normal.cn: 想象一个钓鱼的人，他在等，而不是猛拉。

normal.en: Say ih-LISS-it; the soft s sounds like something slipping out.
normal.cn: 读成 ih-LISS-it，柔和的 s 音像有东西滑出来。

normal.en: Pair it with question: a good question elicits, a bad one forces.
normal.cn: 和 question 配对：好问题引出，坏问题逼出。

abstract.en: What is freely offered is not elicited; the word always implies a small resistance.
abstract.cn: 自愿给出的东西不算被引出；这个词总含一点阻力。

abstract.en: Asking well is the art of making the hidden willing to appear.
abstract.cn: 好好发问，是让隐藏之物愿意出现的艺术。

abstract.en: The response was already there; the question only opened the door.
abstract.cn: 回应本来就在；问题只是开了门。

examples.en: The question elicited a long silence, then a name.
examples.cn: 这个问题先引出沉默，然后引出一个名字。

examples.en: The new rule elicited protests from every department.
examples.cn: 新规定引起每个部门的抗议。

examples.en: The old song elicited a story about his first job.
examples.cn: 那首老歌唤起了一个关于他第一份工作的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: e（向外）+ lic（诱）+ it：把深处的答案诱出来，就是「引出」。

root: 拉丁语 lacere（引诱），加前缀 ex-（向外）→ elicere（诱出）

sensesIntro.en: Elicit always describes a two-way event: something hidden on one side, a skilled touch on the other, and a result that comes out.
sensesIntro.cn: elicit 总描述一个双向事件：一边藏着东西，一边有技巧性的触碰，然后有个结果出来。

core.en: DRAWING OUT WHAT WAS HIDDEN
core.cn: 把隐藏之物拉出来

branches.en: Answers, details and data obtained by asking.
branches.cn: 通过提问得到的回答、细节与数据。

branches.en: Reactions such as protest, applause and anger.
branches.cn: 抗议、掌声与愤怒这类反应。

branches.en: Memories carried back into the present.
branches.cn: 被带回当下的记忆。

branches.en: Small involuntary signs, like a smile.
branches.cn: 微笑这类不由自主的小信号。

branches.en: The same pulling can inform or provoke.
branches.cn: 同一种拉拽，可以告知，也可以激怒。

intro.en: The lic family is about attracting and drawing: elicit draws out, allure attracts, and lace once meant a snare.
intro.cn: lic 词族与吸引、牵引有关：elicit 引出，allure 吸引，而 lace 曾指一道网罗。

latinIntro.en: Latin lacere means to entice; the prefix ex- turns enticement into extraction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lacere 意为引诱；前缀 ex- 把「诱」变成「取出」。

items.example: The test elicited a clear answer.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试引出了一个清楚的答案。

items.example: Her elicitous reply pleased the room.
items.exampleCN: 她得体的回答让全场满意。

items.meaningCN: 不被允许、在法律之外的
items.example: The illicit trade continued at night.

items.exampleCN: 这个报价吸引了许多买家。

items.example: The delicacy melted on the tongue.

definition_zh: 水文循环；以水文学术语表述的水在陆地、海洋与大气间的往复过程
definition_en: the continuous circulation of water through evaporation, atmospheric transport, precipitation, storage and runoff, viewed as a subject of hydrology
core_image: 一张流域剖面图上，雨水从云层落下，一部分入河，一部分下渗，箭头最终回到海洋与云
scene: 水文站的剖面图上，雨线从云里落到山坡，一部分汇入河道，一部分钻进土层。 On the hydrologist's cross-section, the hydrological cycle is drawn as arrows from cloud to slope, river and sea.
sceneCN: 这里 hydrological cycle 指「从水文学角度描述的水在陆地、海洋与大气间的往复」（第 1 个义项：把蒸发、输送、降水、蓄存与径流作为整体研究的水文过程）；句意为在水文工作者的剖面上，这一循环被画成从云到山坡、河流再回到海洋的箭头。可辨识物件：剖面图、云、山坡、河道、下渗箭头。

pos.zh: 水文循环；水循环（学术用语，不可数）

forms.label: 复数（指多个流域或多次循环）

derivatives.zh: 水位（或流量）过程线；水文图

senses.title: The whole cycle as a subject
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的完整循环
senses.definition: the complete set of water transfers treated as one system by hydrology
senses.definitionCN: 水文学把全部水的转移当作一个系统来处理的整体
senses.example: The course begins with the hydrological cycle as a single system.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课先把水文循环当作一个系统来讲。
senses.why: Hydrology needs a name for the object it studies, and that object is not one river or one rainstorm but the whole set of transfers linked into a loop.
senses.whyCN: 水文学需要给它研究的对象一个名字，而这个对象不是某条河或某场暴雨，而是连成回路的整套转移。

senses.title: Evaporation and transpiration
senses.titleCN: 蒸发与蒸腾：水离开水面和植物
senses.definition: the upward loss of water from open water, soil and plant leaves
senses.definitionCN: 水从开阔水面、土壤与植物叶片向上散失的部分
senses.example: In summer, evaporation and transpiration dominate the cycle's upward arm.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季，蒸发与蒸腾主导循环的上升分支。
senses.why: Plants are part of the loop, not bystanders: they pull water from soil and release it through leaves, so the upward arm has two sources.
senses.whyCN: 植物是回路的一部分而非旁观者：它们从土壤吸水、经叶片释放，因此上升分支有两个来源。

senses.title: Atmospheric transport
senses.titleCN: 大气输送：水汽从一个地方移到另一个地方
senses.definition: the movement of vapour by winds from where it evaporated to where it will fall
senses.definitionCN: 水汽被风从其蒸发地移动到其将降落之处的过程
senses.example: Atmospheric transport carries ocean vapour hundreds of kilometres inland.
senses.exampleCN: 大气输送把海洋水汽带到内陆数百公里处。
senses.why: The loop is not local: the place that loses water and the place that receives it are usually far apart, and wind is the link.
senses.whyCN: 这个回路不是局地的：失水的地方与得水的地方通常相距很远，风就是中间的连接。

senses.title: Precipitation over a basin
senses.definition: the return of water to the land or sea surface as rain, snow or hail
senses.definitionCN: 水以雨、雪或冰雹形式回到陆地或海面的部分
senses.example: Precipitation over the basin is measured at a network of gauges.
senses.exampleCN: 流域内的降水由一组雨量计测量。
senses.why: For a hydrologist, rain is an input term in an equation, so it must be measured rather than merely observed.
senses.whyCN: 对水文工作者来说，降雨是方程里的一个输入项，因此必须测量，而不只是「看到下雨」。

senses.title: Storage in soil and rock
senses.titleCN: 蓄存：水停留在土壤与岩层中
senses.definition: water held temporarily in soil moisture, aquifers, lakes, snow and ice
senses.definitionCN: 暂存于土壤水、含水层、湖泊、积雪与冰中的水
senses.example: Storage delays the cycle: water may stay underground for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 蓄存使循环发生延迟：水可能在地下停留数十年。
senses.why: Not every drop moves at the same speed. Storage is the memory of the cycle, and it explains why a dry year can be followed by a wet one.
senses.whyCN: 并非每一滴水都以同样速度移动。蓄存是这个循环的记忆，也解释了为什么旱年之后可能跟着一个湿年。

senses.title: Runoff and discharge
senses.titleCN: 径流与排泄：水离开流域
senses.definition: the water that leaves a basin through streams, rivers and groundwater outflow
senses.definitionCN: 经溪流、河流与地下水流出离开流域的水
senses.example: Discharge at the gauge is the basin's runoff term.
senses.exampleCN: 测站测到的流量就是流域的径流项。
senses.why: Every basin has an exit, and what passes that exit is what the upstream area failed to store or evaporate.
senses.whyCN: 每个流域都有一个出口，通过出口的水就是上游地区没能蓄住或蒸发的部分。

senses.title: The basin-scale balance
senses.titleCN: 流域尺度平衡：把各项写成方程
senses.definition: the equation in which precipitation equals evaporation, runoff and change in storage
senses.definitionCN: 把降水与蒸发、径流和蓄量变化相等的方程
senses.example: The basin-scale balance closed to within five per cent last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年流域尺度的收支平衡误差在百分之五以内。
senses.why: Once every transfer has a name, the loop can be written as an equation, and an equation is what makes prediction possible.
senses.whyCN: 一旦每种转移都有了名字，这个回路就能写成一个方程，而方程正是预测成为可能的原因。

senses.title: The intensified cycle
senses.titleCN: 加强的循环：变暖下的加速
senses.definition: the observed speeding-up of water transfers as the atmosphere warms
senses.definitionCN: 大气变暖后被观测到的水的转移加快
senses.example: A warmer atmosphere intensifies the hydrological cycle, with heavier bursts and longer dry spells.
senses.exampleCN: 更暖的大气加强水文循环，带来更强的暴雨和更长的干旱期。
senses.why: Warm air holds more vapour, so the same loop can carry more water per round; the stages do not change, only their speed and size.
senses.whyCN: 暖空气能容纳更多水汽，因此同一个回路每一轮能搬运更多水；环节不变，只是速度和规模变了。

intro.en: The phrase is Greek in its technical parts and English in its grammar: hydōr supplies the water, logos supplies the study, and cycle supplies the round. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语的技术成分来自希腊语，语法外壳是英语：hydōr 提供「水」，logos 提供「研究」，cycle 提供「一圈」。年代为约数。

items.en: Greek hydōr, genitive hydatos, meant water; English uses the combining form hydro- or hydr-, as in hydrology and hydroelectric.
items.cn: 希腊语 hydōr（属格 hydatos）意为水；英语使用组合形式 hydro- 或 hydr-，如 hydrology 与 hydroelectric。

items.en: Logos meant word, account or reasoned study; the suffix -logia produced names of sciences, and English -logy followed that pattern.
items.cn: logos 指言词、账目或有条理的研究；后缀 -logia 用来构成学科名称，英语 -logy 沿用了这一模式。

items.en: Hydrology, the study of water on the earth, is recorded in English from the seventeenth century, and hydrological is its adjective.
items.cn: hydrology 指研究地球上水的学问，英语自十七世纪起有记载，hydrological 是它的形容词。

items.en: The full phrase hydrological cycle belongs to twentieth-century technical English, when water budgets came to be taught as a single circulating system.
items.cn: 完整的 hydrological cycle 属于二十世纪技术英语，当时水量收支开始被当作一个循环系统来教授。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation): the exact year and author of the first printed use of hydrological cycle cannot be fixed from standard references, so the dating here is a general estimate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：hydrological cycle 首次印刷使用的确切年份与作者无法由通行资料确定，此处年代只是一般估计。

note.en: The first group holds terms built from the same Greek material; the second holds terms that describe parts or neighbours of the same system.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一批希腊语材料构成的术语；第二组是描述同一系统局部或邻近概念的术语。

entries.definition: The same term with the shorter American adjective; the meaning is identical.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的美式短形容词形式，含义完全相同。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the same loop, used in schools rather than in journals.
entries.definitionCN: 同一回路的日常名称，多用于学校而非期刊。

entries.definition: A computer representation of the cycle; the cycle is what the model tries to imitate.
entries.definitionCN: 循环的计算机表示；循环才是模型试图模仿的对象。

entries.definition: The same transfers written as income and outgo, with no emphasis on motion.
entries.definitionCN: 把同样的转移写成收入与支出，不强调运动本身。

entries.definition: The study of the cycle within one catchment, a part rather than the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 研究一个集水区内的循环，是整体的一部分。

entries.definition: Any closed repeated movement; the hydrological cycle is the water case of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何闭合的重复运动；水文循环是它在水的方面的实例。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek pieces, the paired adjective, and the two arms hydrologists actually measure.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语构件、成对的形容词，以及水文工作者真正测量的两条分支。

normal.en: hydro- is Greek for water, so hydrology is literally 'water study'.
normal.cn: hydro- 在希腊语中就是水，所以 hydrology 字面就是「水的学问」。

normal.en: -logy names a science, as in biology, geology and climatology.
normal.cn: -logy 用来命名学科，如生物学、地质学与气候学。

normal.en: The American form drops the -logical ending to -logic: hydrologic cycle.
normal.cn: 美式形式把 -logical 缩为 -logic，成为 hydrologic cycle。

normal.en: Two arms are measured: the upward arm (evaporation plus transpiration) and the downward arm (precipitation).
normal.cn: 被测量的是两条分支：上升分支（蒸发加蒸腾）与下降分支（降水）。

normal.en: A basin closes its accounts: input equals output plus storage change.
normal.cn: 一个流域要平账：输入等于输出加蓄量变化。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the phrase is a machine with no off switch: the same water is reassigned to a new stage forever.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，这个短语是一台没有开关的机器：同一批水永远被重新分配到下一个环节。

abstract.en: It is also a memory system: storage is what lets one season pay for another.
abstract.cn: 它也是一个记忆系统：蓄存让一个季节为另一个季节买单。

abstract.en: Speed is the only variable: warming does not add stages, it only shortens the time each stage takes.
abstract.cn: 速度是唯一的变量：变暖不增添环节，只是缩短每个环节所占的时间。

examples.en: Hydrologists treat the hydrological cycle as a set of linked reservoirs and fluxes.
examples.cn: 水文工作者把水文循环当作一组相连的储库与通量。

examples.en: Urbanisation changes the hydrological cycle by replacing soil with concrete.
examples.cn: 城市化用混凝土取代土壤，从而改变水文循环。

examples.en: The hydrological cycle of a small catchment can be modelled in a few equations.
examples.cn: 一个小集水区的水文循环可以用几个方程来模拟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海卓逻辑（hydro-logic）+ 圈」——用水文的逻辑把水的一圈算清楚 → 水文循环

root: 希腊语 hydōr「水」+ logos「言说、研究」+ kyklos「圆圈」，经拉丁语进入英语，二十世纪构成专业术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same loop as hydrology sees it: the whole system, its upward arm, its transport, its fall, its storage, its exit, its balance, and its recent speed-up.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿水文学所见的同一回路展开：整体系统、上升分支、输送、降落、蓄存、出口、收支平衡，以及近年来的加速。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cross-section with arrows — cloud, slope, river, rock, sea, and back to cloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张带箭头的剖面图——云、山坡、河流、岩层、海洋，再回到云。

branches.en: WHOLE SYSTEM: the term names the object hydrology studies before it names any part.
branches.cn: 整体系统：这个术语先命名水文学研究的对象，再命名其中任何局部。

branches.en: TWO UPWARD LINKS: water leaves by evaporation and transpiration, then travels as vapour.
branches.cn: 两条上升链：水经蒸发与蒸腾离开，再以水汽形式输送。

branches.en: THE INPUT: precipitation is the measurable income of every basin.
branches.cn: 输入项：降水是每个流域可测量的收入。

branches.en: HOLD AND RELEASE: storage delays water, discharge releases it.
branches.cn: 存与放：蓄存让水延迟，排泄把水放出。

branches.en: BALANCE AND SPEED: the loop can be closed as an equation, and warming changes only its rate.
branches.cn: 平衡与速度：这个回路可以写成闭合方程，而变暖只改变它的速率。

intro.en: The phrase is assembled from two Greek morphemes plus one Greek noun for a round, which makes it a readable technical label rather than an opaque borrowing.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个希腊语素加一个表示「一圈」的希腊名词组装而成，因此是可读的技术标签，而不是不透明的借词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved: hydōr is Greek, and Latin itself borrowed the Greek forms hydr- and cyclus. Latin aqua means water but is not the same root, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根：hydōr 是希腊语，拉丁语本身也是借入希腊形式 hydr- 与 cyclus。拉丁语 aqua 虽指水，却不是同一词根，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: the study of the named subject
items.meaningCN: 对所指对象的系统研究

items.meaning: the science of water on and under the earth
items.meaningCN: 研究地表水与地下水的科学
items.example: Hydrology supplies the numbers for water planning.
items.exampleCN: 水文学为水资源规划提供数据。
水文图会标出流域边界。

items.example: A hydrologist measured the river's flow.
items.exampleCN: 一位水文工作者测量了河流的流量。

items.meaning: the water layer of the planet
items.example: The hydrosphere includes ice and vapour.

items.meaning: a plotted record of flow against time
items.meaningCN: 流量随时间变化的绘制记录
items.example: The hydrograph peaks a day after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 流量过程线在暴雨后一天达到峰值。

items.meaning: combined loss of water from soil and plants
items.meaningCN: 土壤与植物共同散失的水
items.example: Evapotranspiration returns half the rain to the air.
items.exampleCN: 蒸散作用把一半的雨水送回空中。

items.example: Precipitation is the cycle's main input.
items.exampleCN: 降水是这一循环的主要输入。

items.meaning: water that flows away over the land
items.example: Runoff carries sediment to the river.

definition_zh: 财务风险；金融风险
definition_en: the risk of losing money through financial transactions, markets or obligations
core_image: 一张资产负债表上有一处正在渗水的裂缝
scene: 货币危机之后，银行重新审查资产负债表，评估汇率波动与坏账可能带来的损失。 The bank reviewed its financial risk after the currency crisis.
sceneCN: 这里指「金融风险」，对应第 1 个义项：因金融交易、市场或债务而蒙受损失的可能；句意为货币危机之后，银行重新审查了自身金融风险。画面要点：资产负债表、汇率曲线、风险审查章。

pos.zh: 财务风险；金融风险（可数指具体一类风险）

senses.title: Exposure to monetary loss
senses.titleCN: 蒙受金钱损失的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility of losing money through financial activities
senses.definitionCN: 因金融活动而损失金钱的可能性
senses.example: The audit found serious financial risk in the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现该子公司存在严重的金融风险。
senses.why: Financial narrows risk to money, so the broad chance of harm becomes a chance of loss measured in currency.
senses.whyCN: financial 把风险收窄到金钱，于是广义的受害概率变成以货币计量的损失概率。

senses.title: Credit risk
senses.definition: the risk that a borrower or counterparty fails to pay
senses.definitionCN: 借款人或交易对手无法付款的风险
senses.example: Credit risk rose as small firms struggled.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业陷入困境，信用风险随之上升。
senses.why: One source of loss is another party's failure, so the general exposure is narrowed to who owes the money.
senses.whyCN: 损失的一个来源是对方违约，于是普遍敞口被收窄到「谁欠着钱」。

senses.title: Market risk
senses.definition: the risk that prices, rates or indices move against a position
senses.definitionCN: 价格、利率或指数朝持仓不利方向变动的风险
senses.example: Market risk dominates a trading book.
senses.exampleCN: 市场风险在交易账簿中占主导。
senses.why: Another source is the market itself, where prices move without anyone defaulting.
senses.whyCN: 另一个来源是市场本身：价格会变动，却没有任何人违约。

senses.title: Liquidity risk
senses.definition: the risk of being unable to meet obligations when they fall due
senses.definitionCN: 到期无法履行义务的风险
senses.example: Liquidity risk can sink a solvent bank.
senses.exampleCN: 流动性风险能拖垮一家仍有偿付能力的银行。
senses.why: The danger is not lack of assets but lack of ready cash, so the word focuses on timing rather than value.
senses.whyCN: 危险不是没有资产，而是没有随时可用的现金，所以这个词聚焦于时点而非价值。

senses.title: Operational risk
senses.definition: the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems or fraud
senses.definitionCN: 流程、人员、系统失败或欺诈造成损失的风险
senses.example: Operational risk includes errors and internal theft.
senses.exampleCN: 操作风险包括差错与内部盗窃。
senses.why: The source moves inside the firm: the machinery and people meant to handle money can themselves fail.
senses.whyCN: 来源移到公司内部：本应处理金钱的机械与人员本身也会失灵。

senses.title: Currency risk
senses.definition: the risk that exchange rates change the value of foreign payments or assets
senses.definitionCN: 汇率变动改变外币付款或资产价值的风险
senses.example: Exporters face currency risk on every contract.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商在每份合同上都面临汇率风险。
senses.why: When money itself changes price across borders, even a safe asset can lose value at home.
senses.whyCN: 当货币本身在跨境之间改变价格，连安全的资产也可能在本国贬值。

senses.title: Systemic risk
senses.definition: the risk that one failure spreads through the whole financial system
senses.definitionCN: 单一失败蔓延至整个金融体系的风险
senses.example: Regulators watch systemic risk across banks.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者监测跨银行的系统性风险。
senses.why: The unit of danger grows from a firm to the system, so a local loss becomes a threat to everyone.
senses.whyCN: 危险的单位从一家机构扩大到整个体系，局部的损失于是成为对所有人的威胁。

senses.title: Risk to capital and earnings
senses.definition: the risk that a firm's capital or earnings fall below what is required
senses.definitionCN: 公司资本或盈利跌破要求水平的风险
senses.example: The quarterly report modelled financial risk against capital.
senses.exampleCN: 季度报告以资本为基准对金融风险作了建模。
senses.why: Risk management compares possible losses with the buffer available, so the exposure is read as a threat to solvency.
senses.whyCN: 风险管理把可能损失与可用缓冲相比较，于是敞口被读成对偿付能力的威胁。

intro.en: Financial risk joins financial, from a French word for settling a debt, with risk, a Romance loan whose deeper origin is disputed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: financial risk 把 financial 与 risk 组合起来：前者出自法语表示结清债务的词，后者是来源有争议的罗曼语借词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant an end or boundary, and it built words about ending, limiting and settling.
items.cn: finis 意为终点或边界，构成了一批表示结束、限定与结清的词。

items.en: Finer meant to settle a debt or bring a matter to an end, from the same notion of a boundary being closed.
items.cn: finer 意为结清债务或把事办完，来自同一个「划上边界」的观念。

items.en: Finance named the payment or settlement of a debt, and English borrowed it for money management in general.
items.cn: finance 指债务的支付或结清，英语借来表示一般意义上的资金管理。

items.en: The adjective financial was formed to describe matters of money, revenue and funding.
items.cn: 形容词 financial 用来描述金钱、收入与筹资事务。

items.en: Risk came through French and Italian; its deeper origin is source uncertain, with a Greek reef explanation and a Latin cutting explanation both unproven.
items.cn: risk 经法语与意大利语而来；更深来源不确定，暗礁说与切掉说都未获证明。

items.en: Twentieth-century regulation split financial risk into credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic types.
items.cn: 二十世纪监管把金融风险分成信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性等类型。

note.en: The first group is built from the same finance root and is easily confused; the second group names particular risks or wider dangers.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「财务」词根上，容易混淆；第二组指具体风险或更广的危险。

entries.definition: The management of money, or to provide funds; it is the field, not the danger within it.
entries.definitionCN: 资金管理，或提供资金；它是领域，而不是领域内的危险。

entries.definition: Relating to money; it describes the kind of risk but does not by itself mean risk.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱有关的；它描述风险的种类，本身并不表示风险。

entries.definition: A person who deals in large sums or arranges funding; it is a role, not a danger.
entries.definitionCN: 处理大额资金或安排融资的人；它是角色，不是危险。

entries.definition: A sum paid as a penalty, or excellent; the penalty sense comes from the idea of settling a matter, not from finance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款，或优秀的；罚款义出自「把事结清」的观念，而非金融本身。

entries.definition: The risk that a borrower defaults; it is one component of financial risk, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 借款人违约的风险；它是金融风险的一个组成部分，而非整个类别。

entries.definition: The risk of loss from price movements; like credit risk, it is a part of the wider financial category.
entries.definitionCN: 价格变动造成损失的风险；与信用风险一样，是更广类别的一部分。

entries.definition: The size of a position affected by a factor; financial risk is the possibility, exposure is the measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 受某因素影响的持仓规模；金融风险是可能性，敞口是被计量的数额。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to pay debts; it is a result that financial risk may produce, not the risk itself.
entries.definitionCN: 无力偿还债务的状态；它是金融风险可能导致的结果，而非风险本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real settling root of finance, the disputed origin of risk, and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「结清」词根、来源有争议的 risk，以及真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Finance began as settling a debt; adding risk turns settlement into possible loss.
normal.cn: finance 最初指结清债务；加上 risk，结清就变成可能的损失。

normal.en: The phrase covers subtypes: credit, market, liquidity, operational, currency and systemic.
normal.cn: 这个短语涵盖多个子类：信用、市场、流动性、操作、汇率与系统性。

normal.en: Credit risk asks who may not pay; market risk asks what prices may do; liquidity risk asks when cash may fail.
normal.cn: 信用风险问谁可能不付钱；市场风险问价格可能怎么走；流动性风险问现金何时会断。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: financial risk management, exposure, systemic financial risk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：金融风险管理、风险敞口、系统性金融风险。

normal.en: Operational risk comes from inside, while systemic risk grows until it reaches everyone.
normal.cn: 操作风险来自内部，系统性风险则扩大到波及所有人。

abstract.en: Picture a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one yet knows how far the leak will spread.
abstract.cn: 想象一张资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，还没人知道会渗多远。

abstract.en: Picture six pipes feeding one tank, each with its own valve that could fail.
abstract.cn: 想象六条管道通向同一只水箱，每条都有自己的阀门可能失灵。

abstract.en: Picture a single bank's stumble drawn as a crack running through a whole wall of banks.
abstract.cn: 想象一家银行的失足被画成一道裂纹，贯穿整面由银行砌成的墙。

examples.en: The treasurer monitors financial risk every week.
examples.cn: 财务主管每周监测金融风险。

examples.en: Diversification lowers financial risk without removing it.
examples.cn: 分散化降低金融风险，但不能消除它。

examples.en: A sudden currency fall can turn a safe loan into financial risk.
examples.cn: 货币骤然下跌能把一笔安全贷款变成金融风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「金钱上的裂缝」——账面上有一处可能漏水 → 金融风险

root: financial 出自法语 finance「债务的结清、支付」，再上溯到拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」；risk 经法语与意大利语而来，更早来源不确定。两者合指因金融活动蒙受损失的可能。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the general chance of monetary loss and then divide it by source: borrower, market, timing, operations, currency and the whole system, ending with capital adequacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的金钱损失概率开始，再按来源划分：借款方、市场、时点、操作、货币与整个体系，最后落在资本充足性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance sheet with one seam leaking, and no one knows how far the leak will spread.
core.cn: 核心意象：资产负债表上有一道缝在渗水，没人知道会渗多远。

branches.en: THE WHOLE EXPOSURE: every financial activity carries a chance of monetary loss.
branches.cn: 整体敞口：每一项金融活动都带有金钱损失的可能。

branches.en: CREDIT: the borrower or counterparty may fail to pay.
branches.cn: 信用：借款人或交易对手可能不付钱。

branches.en: MARKET AND CAPITAL: prices move against positions, and losses eat into the capital buffer.
branches.cn: 市场与资本：价格朝持仓不利方向走，损失侵蚀资本缓冲。

senses.title: A stream that feeds a larger river
senses.titleCN: 支流：汇入更大河流的小水道
senses.definition: a smaller river or stream that flows into a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 汇入更大河流的较小河流或溪流
senses.example: The clear tributary joins the muddy main river without mixing at first.
senses.exampleCN: 清澈的支流汇入浑浊的干流，起初两股水并不混合。
senses.why: the tributary brings its water to a greater river as a subject brings tribute to a lord; the Latin word for a payer of tribute supplied the name.
senses.whyCN: 支流把水交给更大的河，正如属臣把贡品交给君主；命名正是来自拉丁语中「纳贡者」一词。

senses.title: One branch of a river system
senses.definition: a branch of a river system, viewed as one of its feeders
senses.definitionCN: 河系中的一条分支，被视为汇入干流的水道之一
senses.example: The map marks every tributary of the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了三角洲的每一条支流。
senses.why: once the word names one stream, it extends to each branch in the network, so a system is described by its tributaries.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词命名一条水道，就扩展到网络中的每一条分支，于是整个水系用它的支流来描述。

senses.title: A state that pays tribute
senses.titleCN: 纳贡国：向强国交纳贡品的国家
senses.definition: a state that pays tribute to a stronger state in return for protection or toleration
senses.definitionCN: 为换取保护或容许而向更强国家纳贡的国家
senses.example: The small kingdom became a tributary of its powerful neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小王国成了强邻的纳贡国。
senses.why: the political sense is the oldest: a weaker state hands over goods as a stream hands over water.
senses.whyCN: 政治义最古老：弱国交出货物，正如小河交出水量。

senses.title: A ruler who pays tribute
senses.titleCN: 进贡者：交纳贡品的君主
senses.definition: a ruler or people that pays tribute to a superior power
senses.definitionCN: 向更强势力纳贡的君主或族群
senses.example: Tributary princes came to the capital each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 纳贡的诸侯每年春天来到都城。
senses.why: the noun can name the payer as well as the paying state, since both stand in the same subordinate relation.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可指纳贡的国家，也可指纳贡者本人，因为二者处于同样的从属关系。

senses.title: Of a stream: joining a larger one
senses.definition: of or forming a stream that flows into a larger river
senses.definitionCN: 属于或构成汇入更大河流的水道
senses.example: A tributary stream enters the lake from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 一条支流小溪从北面流入湖中。
senses.why: as an adjective the word simply modifies a stream, glacier or channel that joins a larger one.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是修饰汇入更大水体的溪流、冰川或水道。

senses.title: Of tribute: paid to a superior
senses.definition: relating to tribute or to a state that pays it
senses.definitionCN: 与贡品有关的，或指交纳贡品的国家
senses.example: Tributary payments drained the kingdom's treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 纳贡支出耗尽了王国的国库。
senses.why: the adjective keeps the political sense and modifies payments, obligations or territories.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留政治义，用来修饰款项、义务或领地。

senses.title: A smaller source feeding a larger movement
senses.titleCN: 比喻：汇入主流的小支脉
senses.definition: a smaller source or group that adds to a larger movement or body
senses.definitionCN: 为更大运动或更大整体输送力量的小来源或小群体
senses.example: Regional journals are tributaries of the main scientific literature.
senses.exampleCN: 地方期刊是主流科学文献的支流。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the direction: something smaller flows into something larger and is absorbed by it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了方向：较小的东西流入较大的东西并被其吸收。

senses.title: Water and sediment contributed by a branch
senses.titleCN: 水文：支流对干流的水沙补给
senses.definition: the water and sediment that a branch contributes to the main river
senses.definitionCN: 一条分支向干流输送的水量与泥沙
senses.example: Tributaries supply most of the sediment that builds the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 建造三角洲的大部分泥沙由支流提供。
senses.why: hydrology measures what each tributary contributes, so the word can name the contribution itself.
senses.whyCN: 水文学测量每条支流贡献了多少，因此这个词也可命名所贡献的量。

intro.en: Tributary comes from Latin tributarius 'paying tribute', from tributum 'tax, tribute', from tribuere 'to allot, grant, pay', whose root is tribus 'a division of the Roman people'. The river sense is a modern metaphor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tributary 来自拉丁 tributarius「纳贡的」，出 tributum「税、贡」，再出 tribuere「分配、给予」，根源为 tribus「罗马人民的部族划分」。河流义是近代比喻。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tribus named a division of the Roman people. Its own origin is uncertain: the ancient link with tri- 'three' is a tradition rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: tribus 指罗马人民的部族划分。其自身来源不确定：与 tri-「三」的古关联属传统说法，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: From tribus came tribuere 'to divide out, allot, grant, pay', a verb used for assigning shares and for paying what is owed.
items.cn: 由 tribus 得出 tribuere「分出、配给、给予、支付」，用于分配份额与偿付所欠。

items.en: Tributum was the tax or tribute levied on a subject people; the noun kept the sense of something handed over to a superior.
items.cn: tributum 是向属民征收的税或贡；这个名词保留了「交给上位者之物」的意思。

items.en: The adjective tributarius meant paying tribute, and English took it in the fourteenth century for princes and states in that relation.
items.cn: 形容词 tributarius 意为纳贡的；英语在 14 世纪用它指处于这种关系的君主与国家。

items.en: The stream sense appears in the nineteenth century, when geography described branches as paying their water to the main river; the metaphor is exact but the date is approximate.
items.cn: 河流义在 19 世纪出现，当时地理学把分支描述为向干流交纳水量；比喻很确切，但年代只是约数。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of tribus is disputed, and the first citation of the stream sense is not fixed. The political sense is the historically secure one.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代存疑）：tribus 的来源有争议，河流义的最早书证也未确定；政治义是历史上可靠的一支。

note.en: Group one holds words of the tribute family plus one false friend; group two holds ways of naming a stream that joins another.
note.cn: 第一组是 tribute 词族的词外加一个假朋友；第二组是命名「汇入另一水体的小水道」的其他说法。

entries.definition: Goods or money paid by one ruler or state to another as a sign of submission.
entries.definitionCN: 一方君主或国家向另一方交纳以表示臣服的财物。

entries.definition: An elected Roman official who protected the interests of the plebeians; the word is related through tribus.
entries.definitionCN: 古罗马保护平民利益的民选官员；该词经 tribus 与 tributary 同源。

entries.definition: A body or bench that hears and decides cases; it descends from the seat of a tribune.
entries.definitionCN: 审理并裁决案件的机构或法官席；源自保民官的席位。

entries.definition: Great suffering or trouble; it comes from Latin tribulare 'to thresh', not from tribute.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的苦难或磨难；来自拉丁 tribulare「打谷」，与 tribute 无关。

entries.definition: A division of a river, family or organization; a tributary is specifically one that flows into a larger river.
entries.definitionCN: 河流、家族或组织的分支；tributary 特指汇入更大河流的那一支。

entries.definitionCN: 向更大河流或湖泊供水的小溪，强调补给而非等级关系。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers join; it names the junction, not the smaller stream.
entries.definitionCN: 两条河流汇合的地点；它命名汇合处，而非较小的那条河。

entries.definition: Water entering a lake or basin, or the rate at which it enters.
entries.definitionCN: 进入湖泊或盆地的水，或其进入的速率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.

normal.en: tributary = tribut- (tribute) + -ary: a stream that pays its water as tribute.
normal.cn: tributary = tribut-（贡品）+ -ary：把水当作贡品交上去的小河。

normal.en: The political sense is older; the river sense borrows the relation, not the goods.
normal.cn: 政治义更古老；河流义借的是这层关系，而不是货物。

normal.en: tributary, tribute, contribute and distribute all go back to tribuere 'to allot'.
normal.cn: tributary、tribute、contribute、distribute 都可追到 tribuere「分配」。

normal.en: A tributary is always smaller than what it joins; two equal rivers meet at a confluence.
normal.cn: 支流总比它汇入的水体小；两条同等的河相遇处叫汇流点。

normal.en: The adjective is mostly attributive: a tributary stream, a tributary state, rarely a predicative use.
normal.cn: 这个形容词多作定语：a tributary stream、a tributary state，很少作表语。

abstract.en: Every big movement has tributaries: small journals, local scenes and minor languages feeding a larger current.
abstract.cn: 每一种大潮流都有支流：小期刊、地方场景与少数语言为更大的水流补给。

abstract.en: A person's education is a tributary of the main stream of their life, adding water without becoming it.
abstract.cn: 一个人的教育是人生主河道的一条支流，添了水却没有变成主河道。

abstract.en: A rumour is a tributary of fear, small and steady, and it can raise the whole river.
abstract.cn: 谣言是恐惧的支流，细小而持续，却能把整条河抬高。

examples.en: The Missouri is a tributary of the Mississippi.
examples.cn: 密苏里河是密西西比河的一条支流。

examples.en: Several tributaries cut deep valleys into the plateau.
examples.cn: 几条支流在高原上切出深谷。

examples.en: The empire demanded annual tribute from its tributary states.
examples.cn: 帝国每年向纳贡国索取贡品。

root: 源自拉丁 tributarius「纳贡的」，出 tributum「贡税」，再出 tribuere「分配、给予」，根源为 tribus「部族」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of tributary. The physical sense and the political sense are the same relation at two scales: a smaller unit hands over what it has to a larger one.
sensesIntro.cn: tributary 的八个义项。自然义与政治义是同一关系在两个尺度上的体现：较小的一方把自己所有的交给较大的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small channel runs beside a great river and then gives it all its water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条小水道沿大河旁边流，最后把全部水量交给它。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL STREAM: the feeder itself, then the same word used as an adjective.
branches.cn: 自然水道：先是支流本身，再是同形形容词的用法。

branches.en: NETWORK AND CONTRIBUTION: each branch in the system, then the water and sediment it delivers.
branches.cn: 网络与贡献：系统中的每条分支，再是它输送的水与泥沙。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL RELATION: the subordinate state, then the ruler who pays.
branches.cn: 政治关系：先是属国，再是纳贡的君主。

branches.en: THE ADJECTIVE OF TRIBUTE: payments and obligations, with no river present.
branches.cn: 贡赋的形容词用法：款项与义务，此时没有河流。

branches.en: METAPHOR OF FEEDING: any small source that adds to a larger movement.
branches.cn: 补给隐喻：任何为更大运动添力的小来源。

intro.en: Tributary divides as tribut- plus -ary. The stem is the participle of Latin tribuere 'to allot'; -ary marks relation, so the word means 'relating to tribute'.
intro.cn: tributary 可切分为 tribut- 加 -ary。词干是拉丁 tribuere「分配」的分词形式；-ary 标记关系，因此整个词意为「与贡赋有关的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere yields a large English family: tribute, tributary, contribute, contribution, distribute, distribution and attribution. They share the idea of assigning a share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribuere 衍生出庞大的英语词族：tribute、tributary、contribute、contribution、distribute、distribution、attribution。它们共享「分配份额」的意思。
