pos.zh: 车轴；轮轴

senses.title: The rod a wheel turns on
senses.definition: a rod or spindle passing through the centre of a wheel so that the wheel can rotate
senses.definitionCN: 穿过轮心的杆或轴，使车轮能够旋转
senses.example: The wheel spun freely on its axle.
senses.exampleCN: 车轮在轴上自由转动。
senses.why: Axle descends from a Norse word for the same rod, kin to axis, so the core is always the line a thing turns about.
senses.whyCN: axle 出自指同一根杆的诺斯语词，与 axis 同源，因此核心始终是「物体绕之转动的那条线」。

senses.title: The whole wheel assembly
senses.definition: in vehicle work, the shaft together with its bearings and the two wheels it carries
senses.definitionCN: 在车辆维修中，指轴连同轴承及其所带动的两个车轮
senses.example: They replaced the axle after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞后他们更换了整个轮轴总成。
senses.why: Because the rod is never found bare on a car, the name spread to the whole unit a mechanic removes.
senses.whyCN: 因为在汽车上这根杆从不单独存在，这个名称便扩展到修车师傅整体拆下的那个部件。

intro.en: Axle comes from Old Norse oxull, axle, from a Germanic root also behind axis and the Old English eax, all meaning the line a wheel turns on.
intro.cn: axle 来自古诺斯语 oxull「车轴」，出自同一日耳曼词根，axis 与古英语 eax 亦由此而来，都指车轮绕之转动的那条线。

items.en: A root meaning axle or shoulder joint gave words for the pivot a limb or wheel turns on.
items.cn: 一个表示「轴、肩关节」的词根产生了肢体或车轮绕之转动的枢轴类词。

items.en: Latin axis named an axle and also the line of the heavens, giving English axis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 axis 既指车轴，也指天球的轴线，产生英语 axis。

items.en: Old English eax meant axle, the native form that later lost ground.
items.cn: 古英语 eax 意为「车轴」，是后来退让的本族形式。

items.en: Old Norse oxull named the same rod and supplied the northern English form.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 oxull 指同一根杆，提供了英格兰北部的形式。

items.en: Middle English axeltre named the beam joining two wheels, from oxull plus tre, tree or beam.
items.cn: 中古英语 axeltre 指连接两轮的横梁，由 oxull 加 tre「木、梁」构成。

items.en: The shorter axle is recorded from the seventeenth century and became the workshop word.
items.cn: 较短的 axle 自十七世纪有记载，成为车间用语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the axis family; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring parts of a wheel assembly.
note.cn: 形近组保留 axis 词族；近义组列出轮轴总成上相邻的部件。

entries.definition: The line a body turns about.
entries.definitionCN: 物体绕之转动的线。

entries.definition: Along or about an axis.
entries.definitionCN: 沿轴或绕轴的。

entries.definition: A skating jump named after a man.
entries.definitionCN: 以人名命名的滑冰跳跃。

entries.definition: A passage between rows of seats.
entries.definitionCN: 座排之间的通道。

entries.definition: A slender rod that turns.
entries.definitionCN: 转动的细杆。

entries.definition: A long rod transmitting motion.
entries.definitionCN: 传递运动的长杆。

entries.definition: The centre of a wheel.
entries.definitionCN: 车轮的中心。

entries.definition: A part that lets a shaft turn.
entries.definitionCN: 让轴转动的部件。

normalIntro.en: Axle is kin to axis: the line a wheel turns on, and then the whole unit built around that line.
normalIntro.cn: axle 与 axis 同源：车轮绕之转动的那条线，进而指围绕这条线造出的整个部件。

normal.en: Rear axle and front axle are the usual pairs.
normal.cn: rear axle 与 front axle 是常见的一对。

normal.en: Axle grease is a set workshop phrase.
normal.cn: axle grease 是固定车间用语。

normal.en: Axis is the line, axle is the part.
normal.cn: axis 是那条线，axle 是那个件。

normal.en: The plural is axles, not axies.
normal.cn: 复数是 axles，不是 axies。

normal.en: Axletree is the older, longer name.
normal.cn: axletree 是更早、更长的名称。

abstract.en: Picture an iron rod through a wooden wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁杆穿过木轮。

abstract.en: Imagine the wheel spinning while the rod stays.
abstract.cn: 想象轮在转而杆不动。

abstract.en: Think of one beam carrying two wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁带动两个轮子。

examples.en: Grease the axle before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途行驶前给车轴上润滑脂。

examples.en: The front axle took the whole impact.
examples.cn: 前轴承受了全部撞击。

examples.en: Both axles were bent beyond repair.
examples.cn: 两根车轴都弯得无法修复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ax（与 axis 同族，「轴」）+ -le「小部件」——穿过轮心的那根轴杆，就是 axle。

root: 印欧词根表「轴、枢轴」，拉丁语 axis 与古英语 eax 由此而来；古诺斯语 oxull 加 tre「梁」成中古英语 axeltre，十七世纪缩为 axle。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses centre on one turning line: the rod itself, and the whole assembly a workshop lifts out around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都围绕一条转动之线：杆本身，以及车间围绕它整体吊出的那套部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron rod through the wheel heart that lets it spin
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过轮心让轮子转起来的那根铁杆

branches.en: A wheel spinning on its rod.
branches.cn: 在杆上转动的车轮。

branches.en: Grease applied before a drive.
branches.cn: 行车前涂上的润滑脂。

branches.en: A rear unit replaced after a crash.
branches.cn: 碰撞后更换的后轴总成。

branches.en: Two bent units beyond repair.
branches.cn: 弯得无法修复的两套总成。

branches.en: Both are built about one turning line.
branches.cn: 两者都围绕一条转动之线构成。

intro.en: Axle is ax plus the tool ending -le; the same ax root gives axis and axial, while -tree marked the older beam.
intro.cn: axle 是 ax 加工具词尾 -le；同一 ax 词根产生 axis 与 axial，而 -tree 标记了更早的横梁。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is axis, axle or heavenly line; Greek axon gives the same idea, and Latin rota, wheel, gives rotate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 axis「车轴、天轴」；希腊语 axon 给出同一概念，拉丁语 rota「轮」产生 rotate。

latinEntries.exampleCN: axon 给出生物学中的轴突。

definition_zh: 洋底；大洋底部（尤指开阔深海的底部表面）
definition_en: the bottom of the open ocean, especially the deep-sea floor beyond the continental margins
core_image: 越过大陆架的浅水之后，海底像一张巨大的褐色平原一直铺到对面的大陆坡
scene: 科考船拖着声呐，屏幕上一片平坦的褐色缓缓展开。 The sonar revealed a wide plain on the ocean floor.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean floor 指「开阔大洋底部的表面」（第 1 个义项：深海平原所在的洋底）；句意为声呐揭示出洋底一片宽广的平原。图中可辨识物件：声呐缆、屏幕剖面、褐色平原、科考船。

pos.zh: 洋底；大洋底部（通常作单数，带定冠词）

collocations.zh: 洋底（带定冠词的常用形式）

senses.title: Bottom of the open ocean
senses.definition: the bottom surface of the open ocean beyond the shelf and slope
senses.definitionCN: 陆架与陆坡之外的开阔大洋底部表面
senses.example: The sonar revealed a wide plain on the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 声呐揭示出洋底一片宽广的平原。
senses.why: ocean names the open sea and floor names its bottom, so the phrase makes the deep setting explicit in a way seafloor need not.
senses.whyCN: ocean 指开阔海洋，floor 指其底部，因此这个短语比 seafloor 更明确地点出深海环境。

senses.title: Submarine relief
senses.definition: the shape of the deep bottom, including abyssal plains, hills, ridges and trenches
senses.definitionCN: 深海底部的形状，包括深海平原、丘陵、海岭与海沟
senses.example: The map shows seamounts rising from the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 地图显示海山从洋底升起。
senses.why: once mapped, the deep bottom is read as landscape, so the phrase takes on a terrain sense.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被测绘，深海底部就被读作地貌，因此这个短语带上了地形义。

senses.title: Surface of oceanic crust
senses.definition: the upper boundary of the crust that lies under the open ocean
senses.definitionCN: 开阔大洋之下洋壳的上边界
senses.example: Basalt makes up most of the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 玄武岩构成洋底的大部分。
senses.why: geology separates the water from the rock below, and that contact is the ocean floor.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把水体与下方岩石分开，而二者的接触面就是洋底。

senses.title: Record of seafloor spreading
senses.definition: the bottom as the archive of crust formed at mid-ocean ridges
senses.definitionCN: 作为洋中脊所形成洋壳档案的底部
senses.example: Magnetic stripes on the ocean floor record reversals of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 洋底的磁条带记录了地磁倒转。
senses.why: new bottom is created at ridges and moves outward, so the ocean floor carries a dated record of its own growth.
senses.whyCN: 新的洋底在海岭生成并向外移动，因此洋底带着自身生长的可定年记录。

senses.title: Accumulated deep-sea sediment
senses.definition: the layer of pelagic clay, ooze and debris that settles on the deep bottom
senses.definitionCN: 沉降在深海底部的大洋黏土、软泥与碎屑层
senses.example: Slow accumulation covers much of the old ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的堆积覆盖了大部分古老洋底。
senses.why: the deep bottom is a quiet receiver of falling material, so the phrase also names the sediment cover.
senses.whyCN: 深海底部安静地承接落下的物质，因此这个短语也指沉积覆盖层。

senses.title: Deep-sea habitat
senses.definition: the environment of the deep bottom, including vent communities and soft-sediment fauna
senses.definitionCN: 深海底部的环境，包括喷口群落与软沉积物动物群
senses.example: Life on the ocean floor survives without sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 洋底的生命在没有阳光的条件下存活。
senses.why: the deep floor is a place where organisms live, so the phrase can name a habitat rather than a rock surface.
senses.whyCN: 深海底是生物生活的地方，因此这个短语可指栖息地而非岩石表面。

senses.title: Ground for deep-sea resources
senses.definition: the bottom considered as the site of nodules, crusts and other deep-sea deposits
senses.definitionCN: 作为结核、结壳与其他深海矿床所在地的底部
senses.example: Nodules lie scattered across parts of the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 结核散落在洋底的一些区域。
senses.why: industry looks at the bottom as a store of minerals, adding a resource sense to the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 工业把洋底看作矿产储藏，于是给这个短语添上资源义。

senses.title: Object of hydrographic survey
senses.definition: the bottom as the target of echo sounding and bathymetric mapping
senses.definitionCN: 作为回声测深与水深测绘目标的底部
senses.example: The survey vessel spent the summer mapping the ocean floor.
senses.exampleCN: 勘测船花了一个夏天测绘洋底。
senses.why: surveying treats the deep bottom as a surface to be measured, which is a distinct practical sense.
senses.whyCN: 测绘把深海底当作待测量的表面，这构成一个独立的实用义项。

intro.en: Ocean floor joins ocean, from Greek ōkeanos through Latin oceanus, with floor, from Old English flor 'ground, bottom'. The phrase belongs to modern oceanography. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean floor 由 ocean 与 floor 组合而成：ocean 经拉丁 oceanus 来自希腊 ōkeanos，floor 来自古英语 flor「地面、底部」。这个短语属于现代海洋学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ōkeanos was the great river believed to encircle the world, and also its divine name. Its own origin is uncertain and may be non-Greek.
items.cn: ōkeanos 是古人相信环绕大地的巨流，也是它的神名。它自身的来源不确定，可能并非希腊语。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as oceanus, the outer sea, and passed it through French into English as ocean.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 oceanus，指外海，再经法语以 ocean 进入英语。

items.en: Floor comes from Old English flor 'floor, ground, bottom', a Germanic word also used for the bottom of natural features.
items.cn: floor 来自古英语 flor「地板、地面、底部」，这个日耳曼语词也用于自然事物的底部。

items.en: The phrase ocean floor became standard when nineteenth- and twentieth-century expeditions began systematic sounding of the deep sea.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的考察开始系统测深之后，ocean floor 这一短语成为标准说法。

items.en: With plate tectonics the phrase gained its modern geological reading: the top of oceanic crust and the record of spreading.
items.cn: 随着板块构造学说，这个短语获得现代地质含义：洋壳顶面与扩张记录。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of ōkeanos is unsettled, and the pre-Germanic root of floor is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ōkeanos 的来源未有定论，floor 在日耳曼语之前的词根是重构而非有书证的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the oceanic terms that overlap with ocean floor; group two holds words for depth and bottom that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组区分与 ocean floor 重叠的海洋术语；第二组是表示深度与底部的词，范围不同。

entries.definition: The general term for any sea bottom; ocean floor usually points to the deep open ocean rather than a shelf sea.
entries.definitionCN: 任何海洋底部的通称；ocean floor 通常指开阔深海，而非陆架浅海。

entries.definition: The bottom viewed as land, common in law and industry; it lacks the deep-ocean focus of ocean floor.
entries.definitionCN: 把底部视为土地的词，常见于法律与工业；它没有 ocean floor 那种深海指向。

entries.definition: The basalt-rich rock layer under the sea; its top is the ocean floor, but the crust includes the rock below.
entries.definitionCN: 海底之下富含玄武岩的岩石层；它的顶面是洋底，但洋壳还包括下方岩石。

entries.definition: A large depression holding an ocean, including the water and the bottom; ocean floor names only the bottom surface.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳大洋的大型洼地，包括水体与底部；ocean floor 只指底部表面。

entries.definition: The lowest part of anything; without ocean it could mean a box or a page.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最低部分；没有 ocean 时也可指箱子或书页的底部。

entries.definition: The deep water as a region; it names the volume above the bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 作为区域的深水；它指底部上方的水体积。

entries.definition: A bottomless or very deep place; it is more dramatic and less technical than ocean floor.
entries.definitionCN: 无底或极深之处；比 ocean floor 更具戏剧性，也更不技术化。

entries.definition: The whole deep-water environment, including water and bottom; ocean floor selects only the base.
entries.definitionCN: 整个深水环境，包括水与底部；ocean floor 只取基底。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ocean 'open sea' + floor 'bottom': the open sea given a floor.
normal.cn: ocean「开阔海洋」+ floor「底部」：给开阔海洋配一块地板。

normal.en: The related terms run ocean floor, seafloor, seabed, ocean basin and oceanic crust.
normal.cn: 相关术语包括 ocean floor、seafloor、seabed、ocean basin 与 oceanic crust。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: ocean floor spreading, ocean floor sediment, ocean floor mapping.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：洋底扩张、洋底沉积物、洋底测绘。

normal.en: The phrase usually takes the definite article: on the ocean floor.
normal.cn: 这个短语通常带定冠词：on the ocean floor。

normal.en: It is the deep counterpart of continental shelf, the shallow shelf on the other side of the slope.
normal.cn: 它是大陆架在深海的对应物，而大陆架位于陆坡的另一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a brown plain so large that a ship above it seems to hang over nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一片褐色平原大得让上方的船像悬在虚空之上。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are stripes of magnetised rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架由带磁的岩石条带做成。

abstract.en: Picture a darkness where animals make their own light.
abstract.cn: 想象一片黑暗，动物在那里自己发光。

examples.en: The expedition mapped a new section of the ocean floor.
examples.cn: 考察队测绘了洋底的新区域。

examples.en: Sediment on the ocean floor holds a long climate record.
examples.cn: 洋底沉积物保存着漫长的气候记录。

examples.en: The ridge raises new ocean floor above the surrounding plain.
examples.cn: 海岭把新的洋底抬升到周围平原之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ocean（大洋）+ floor（地板）」——大洋的地板就是洋底

root: ocean 经拉丁 oceanus 来自希腊 ōkeanos「环绕大地的巨流」，其来源不确定；floor 来自古英语 flor「地板、地面」；短语属现代海洋学用语，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one deep floor: the open-ocean bottom, its relief, the crust below, the spreading record, the sediment cover, its life, its minerals and its role as a surveyed surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一块深海底展开：开阔洋底、其起伏、其下洋壳、扩张记录、沉积覆盖、其生命、其矿产，以及其作为被测表面的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an enormous brown plain lying under miles of open water.
core.cn: 核心意象：数英里开阔水体之下的一片巨大褐色平原。

branches.en: DEEP GROUND: the open bottom and the sediment that settles on it.
branches.cn: 深部地面：开阔底部与沉降其上的沉积物。

branches.en: SHAPED ROCK: relief and crustal top are one surface seen two ways.
branches.cn: 有形的岩石：地形与洋壳顶面是同一表面的两种看法。

branches.en: GROWING ARCHIVE: magnetic stripes date the bottom's own creation.
branches.cn: 生长的档案：磁条带为洋底自身的生成定年。

branches.en: LIVING DEEP: vent communities and soft-bottom animals inhabit the floor.
branches.cn: 活的深海：喷口群落与软底动物栖居其上。

branches.en: MEASURED STORE: the floor is both a mineral deposit and a survey target.
branches.cn: 被测量的储藏：洋底既是矿床，也是测绘对象。

intro.en: Ocean floor combines a Greek-derived noun with a Germanic one, so its family mixes classical compounds with plain English forms.
intro.cn: ocean floor 把一个希腊来源名词与一个日耳曼语名词组合起来，因此其词族混合了古典复合词与朴素英语形式。

latinIntro.en: Greek ōkeanos passed into Latin as oceanus, which gives ocean and oceanic; floor is Germanic and contributes no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 ōkeanos 进入拉丁语作 oceanus，由此衍生 ocean 与 oceanic；floor 属日耳曼语，不提供拉丁条目。

items.example: The ocean stretched beyond the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 海洋一直延伸到地平线之外。

items.example: The floor of the valley was flat.

items.meaning: the bottom of the open ocean
items.example: The probe reached the ocean floor.

items.exampleCN: 洋底岩石主要是玄武岩。

items.example: She studied oceanography at the coastal institute.
items.exampleCN: 她在海岸研究所学习海洋学。

items.meaning: a large depression holding an ocean
items.meaningCN: 容纳大洋的大型洼地；洋盆
items.example: The Pacific is the deepest ocean basin.

items.structure: Oceanus (Latin proper noun from Greek ōkeanos)
items.meaning: the encircling river of Greek myth
items.meaningCN: 希腊神话中环绕大地的巨流
items.example: Oceanus was imagined as a river around the world.
items.exampleCN: 古人把 oceanus 想象成环绕世界的河流。

latinEntries.meaning: the outer sea; the god Oceanus

definition_zh: 大胆的；放肆的；敢于冒险的；出格的
definition_en: showing a willingness to take bold or surprising risks; showing too much confidence or disrespect
core_image: 明知不该却偏要迈出那一步的人：既有胆量，也有点冒犯
scene: 颁奖礼上，无名新人竟当众指出评委的方案漏洞。 An audacious young architect questioned the judges' design in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 audacious 指「大胆敢言、近乎放肆的」（第 1 个义项：敢作敢当的胆量）；句意：一个胆大包天的年轻建筑师当众质疑评委的设计。

pos.zh: 大胆的；敢于冒险的；放肆的

derivatives.zh: 大胆；放肆（audacious + -ity 名词后缀）
大胆地；放肆地（audacious + -ly 副词后缀）
大胆；放肆（audacious + -ness 名词后缀）
拉丁语原词「大胆的」（仅用于学名与引文）

senses.title: Bold and willing to take risks
senses.definition: showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks
senses.definitionCN: 表现出敢于承担惊人风险的胆量的
senses.example: It was audacious of them to launch the company with no money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们身无分文就敢开公司，真是胆大。
senses.why: The Latin root audax means bold; the core image is the courage to step where others hesitate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 audax 意为「大胆」；核心意象是敢在别人犹豫之处迈步的胆量。

senses.title: Showing disrespect or lack of shame
senses.definition: showing too much confidence or a lack of respect, often in a shocking way
senses.definitionCN: 表现出过分的自信或不敬，常令人震惊的
senses.example: She had the audacious nerve to ask for a raise on her first day.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一天上班就敢开口要加薪，实在放肆。
senses.why: The same boldness can offend when it crosses social lines; the word keeps both faces.
senses.whyCN: 同样的胆量一旦越过社会界线便会冒犯人；这个词始终保有两张面孔。

senses.title: Original and striking in style
senses.definition: of art, fashion, or ideas, strikingly original and unconventional
senses.definitionCN: （艺术、时尚、思想）极其新颖、不循常规的
senses.example: The director made an audacious film with no dialogue at all.
senses.exampleCN: 导演拍了一部全程无对白的大胆电影。
senses.why: In creative fields, breaking rules is the visible form of daring, so the word drifted to style.
senses.whyCN: 在创作领域，打破常规是胆识最直观的形态，词义于是滑向风格。

senses.title: Of actions of breathtaking daring
senses.definition: of a crime, plan, or exploit, so bold that it amazes people
senses.definitionCN: （罪行、计划、壮举）大胆到令人咋舌的
senses.example: The museum theft was an audacious daytime raid.
senses.exampleCN: 那起博物馆失窃案是一次光天化日下的胆大行窃。
senses.why: When daring is aimed at forbidden goals, admiration and shock mix in one word.
senses.whyCN: 当胆量瞄准禁忌目标时，惊叹与震骇便在同一词中交织。

senses.title: Cheeky or impudent in speech
senses.titleCN: 嘴上冒犯的；没大没小的
senses.definition: of a remark or question, rude in a bold, often amusing way
senses.definitionCN: （言辞、提问）大胆而近乎无礼、常带滑稽感的
senses.example: The child asked the audacious question everyone else avoided.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子问出了所有大人都在回避的大胆问题。
senses.why: Children and comedians borrow this boldness harmlessly, giving the word a lighter shade.
senses.whyCN: 孩子和喜剧演员把这份胆量用得毫无恶意，词义因此添了一层轻松色彩。

senses.title: Defying the odds
senses.titleCN: 逆势而为的；明知不可为而为之的
senses.definition: undertaken despite overwhelming difficulty or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 不顾压倒性的困难或反对而进行的
senses.example: Their audacious escape from the besieged city became legend.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从被围之城大胆出逃，成了传奇。
senses.why: Real daring shows itself only against odds, so the word attaches to improbable ventures.
senses.whyCN: 真正的胆识只有在悬殊的劣势前才显形，词义便落在那些看似不可能的行动上。

senses.title: Confident to the point of arrogance
senses.definition: marked by confidence so high it seems like arrogance
senses.definitionCN: 自信过头、近乎傲慢的
senses.example: He closed his speech with an audacious promise to end poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一句终结贫困的大话结束了演讲。
senses.why: When the bold voice exceeds its evidence, listeners hear arrogance rather than courage.
senses.whyCN: 当大胆的宣言超出证据所能支撑时，听者听到的就是傲慢而非勇气。

senses.title: Admirably inventive
senses.definition: of a solution or stroke, daring in a way that earns admiration
senses.definitionCN: （解法、妙手）因敢于打破常规而赢得赞叹的
senses.example: The audacious final move won the chess match.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那步大胆的走法赢下了棋局。
senses.why: The bright side of audax is creative risk-taking; chess and strategy keep it alive.
senses.whyCN: audax 光明的一面是创造性的冒险；棋局与谋略让这层意思留存至今。

intro.en: Audacious comes from the Latin adjective audax, bold, built on audere, to dare; English borrowed it through the related noun audacia in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: audacious 源自拉丁语形容词 audax「大胆的」，其核心是动词 audere「敢」；16 世纪英语经由相关名词 audacia 借入该词。

items.en: The root *awej- meant to be eager or to dare, pointing toward bold desire and confidence.
items.cn: 词根 *awej- 意为「渴望、敢于」，指向大胆的欲望与自信。

items.en: audere meant to dare, and its adjective audax (genitive audacis) meant bold or daring.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audere 意为「敢」，其形容词 audax（属格 audacis）意为「大胆的、敢作敢为的」。

items.en: The noun audacia meant boldness, both the noble courage and the shameless forwardness.
items.cn: 名词 audacia 意为「大胆」，兼指高尚的勇气与无耻的放肆。

items.en: English took audacious and audacity together in the mid-sixteenth century, keeping the double sense of courage and impudence.
items.cn: 16 世纪中叶英语同时借入 audacious 与 audacity，勇气与无礼的双重意味一并保留。

items.en: Writers used it of bold soldiers and of presumptuous claims alike, fixing the word's two faces.
items.cn: 作家既用它写勇猛的将士，也用它写狂妄的断言，双面含义就此固定。

items.en: Modern usage praises audacious artists and entrepreneurs while still using it to scold the rude.
items.cn: 现代用法既赞艺术家的胆识、创业者的果敢，也仍用它斥责无礼之人。

note.en: Group one collects look-alikes from the dare family and words sharing the aud- spelling by accident; group two collects neighboring bold words.
note.cn: 第一组收「敢」字族及拼写恰好同以 aud- 开头的词；第二组收相邻的大胆类词。

entries.definition: the noun form: boldness or shameless daring.
entries.definitionCN: audacious 的名词形式：大胆；放肆。

entries.definition: able to be heard, from Latin audire, to hear; only the aud- spelling is shared.
entries.definitionCN: 听得见的，出自拉丁语 audire「听」；只是拼写同以 aud- 开头，词源不同。

entries.definition: relating to sound; from the hear root, not the dare root.
entries.definitionCN: 音频的；出自「听」的词根，与「敢」的词根无关。

entries.definition: majestic and venerable, from Latin augere, to increase; not from audax.
entries.definitionCN: 威严的；令人敬畏的，出自拉丁语 augere「增长」，与 audax 无关。

entries.definition: fearless and adventurous; the plain everyday term.
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢的；大胆的；最常用的日常说法。

entries.definition: adventurously courageous, often admiring.
entries.definitionCN: 勇于冒险的；多含赞赏之意。

entries.definition: bold without shame; heavier on the impudence side.
entries.definitionCN: 厚颜无耻的；更侧重无礼一面。

entries.definition: fearless, especially of explorers and heroes.
entries.definitionCN: 无畏的；多用于探险家与英雄。

entries.definition: bold without thought of danger or consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽的；不计后果的大胆，多含贬义。

normalIntro.en: audacious keeps its Latin heart audax, bold, visible in audacity and the aud- spelling.
normalIntro.cn: audacious 保留拉丁语心脏 audax「大胆」，在 audacity 与 aud- 拼写中清晰可见。

normal.en: audax to audacious: dare first, then add the adjective ending.
normal.cn: 从 audax 到 audacious：先「敢」，再加形容词词尾。

normal.en: The -acious ending recurs in tenacious and vivacious, all meaning full of something.
normal.cn: -acious 词尾常见于 tenacious、vivacious，都表示「充满某性质」。

normal.en: audacity is the noun you reach for when someone dares too much.
normal.cn: 当某人胆子太大时，你会脱口而出它的名词 audacity。

normal.en: An audacious plan is bold enough to make people gasp.
normal.cn: 大胆的计划胆量大到让人倒吸一口气。

normal.en: Its twin senses: courage you admire, nerve you scold.
normal.cn: 双生含义：一面是你赞赏的勇气，一面是你训斥的放肆。

abstract.en: Picture someone stepping off a cliff-edge ledge others refuse to touch.
abstract.cn: 想象有人踩上众人不敢碰的悬崖边缘。

abstract.en: The word itself leans forward, like a hand raised before permission is given.
abstract.cn: 这个词本身向前倾，像未经允许就先举起的手。

abstract.en: Audacious is a tightrope between hero and nuisance.
abstract.cn: audacious 是英雄与讨厌鬼之间的一根钢丝。

examples.en: It was audacious of the junior clerk to rewrite the director's report.
examples.cn: 那个小职员胆子真大，竟敢重写主管的报告。

examples.en: The audacious jailbreak was planned in a single night.
examples.cn: 这场胆大包天的越狱仅一夜之间便策划完成。

examples.en: Critics praised the band's audacious blend of opera and punk.
examples.cn: 评论家盛赞该乐队将歌剧与朋克大胆融合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「傲地死」——傲慢到地上打滚也要坚持大胆发言，胆大放肆到极点

root: 出自拉丁语 audax「大胆的」（属格 audacis），核心为动词 audere「敢」；经其派生名词 audacia「大胆；放肆」于 16 世纪进入英语，与 audacity 同族，属「敢」词根一系，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all grow from one root meaning bold: from admired courage through impudent nerve to inventive brilliance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「大胆」这一词根生长：从受人赞叹的勇气，到近乎无礼的放肆，再到令人叫绝的独创。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping forward when everyone else steps back.
core.cn: 核心意象：众人后退时，偏要向前迈出一步。

branches.en: THE COURAGE SIDE: bold ventures and improbable escapes.
branches.cn: 勇气一面：大胆的事业与看似不可能的出逃。

branches.en: THE NERVE SIDE: remarks and demands that cross the line.
branches.cn: 放肆一面：越界的言辞与要求。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE SIDE: art and moves that break rules and win praise.
branches.cn: 创造一面：打破常规、赢得赞叹的艺术与妙手。

branches.en: THE CRIME SIDE: exploits so bold they amaze.
branches.cn: 惊世一面：大胆到令人咋舌的行径。

branches.en: THE ARROGANCE SIDE: confidence that outruns its proof.
branches.cn: 傲慢一面：超出证据的自信。

intro.en: audacious is audax plus -acious, an adjective ending meaning full of; the dare root is the whole engine of the word.
intro.cn: audacious 由 audax 加 -acious 构成，后者是表示「充满某性质」的形容词词尾；「敢」的词根是全词的发动机。

latinIntro.en: Latin audere, to dare, is the anchor: audax, audacia, and English audacious and audacity all descend from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audere「敢」是家族之锚：audax、audacia，以及英语的 audacious、audacity 皆出于此。

definition_zh: 水陆两栖的；水陆两用的；兼具两种活动领域能力的
definition_en: able to live or operate both in water and on land
core_image: 脚踏两只世界的青蛙：水里能游，岸上能跳
scene: 登陆艇冲上沙滩，舱门放下，士兵与战车鱼贯而出。 The army launched an amphibious assault at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里的 amphibious 是「水陆两用的」（第 3 个义项：军事上跨越水陆两域作战）；句意是军队在黎明发起两栖登陆进攻。

pos.zh: 水陆两栖的
水陆两用的；两栖作战的

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「两栖动物；两栖飞机」
形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「水陆两栖地」
同前缀词（amphi- 表「两」），义为「歧义句；结构含混的表述」

senses.title: Able to live both in water and on land
senses.titleCN: 水陆两栖的：动物双栖能力
senses.definition: of animals, especially frogs and salamanders, capable of living in water and on land
senses.definitionCN: 指蛙、蝾螈等动物既能水中生活也能陆地生活
senses.example: Frogs are the most familiar amphibious creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙是我们最熟悉的两栖动物。
senses.why: The Greek amphi means both ways and bios means life: a double life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 amphi 意为「双向」，bios 意为「生命」：即过双重生活。

senses.title: Of plants growing in both water and soil
senses.titleCN: 水陆两生的：植物双环境生长
senses.definition: of plants able to grow in water or in wet soil
senses.definitionCN: 能在水中或湿地土壤中生长的植物属性
senses.example: Rice is essentially an amphibious plant.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻本质上是一种水陆两生植物。
senses.why: The double-life idea transfers from animals to anything that straddles both worlds.
senses.whyCN: 「双重生活」的观念从动物转移到任何横跨两个世界的事物。

senses.title: Of military operations crossing sea and land
senses.titleCN: 两栖作战的：跨越海陆的军事行动
senses.definition: of military forces or operations launched from sea onto land
senses.definitionCN: 指由海向陆发起的军事力量或行动
senses.example: The allies trained for months before the amphibious landing.
senses.exampleCN: 盟军为两栖登陆训练了数月。
senses.why: Soldiers, like frogs, must cross the waterline; war borrowed the zoology term.
senses.whyCN: 士兵如青蛙必须跨越水线，军事领域借用了动物学术语。

senses.title: Of vehicles and aircraft operating on water and land
senses.titleCN: 水陆两用的：交通工具跨域运行
senses.definition: of vehicles or aircraft designed to operate on both water and land
senses.definitionCN: 指设计为可在水面与陆地运行的载具
senses.example: The amphibious truck drove straight off the beach into the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆水陆两用卡车从沙滩径直驶入海湾。
senses.why: Engineering gave machines the frog's trick, and kept the frog's word.
senses.whyCN: 工程学赋予机器青蛙的本领，也沿用了青蛙的名称。

senses.title: Operating in two distinct realms or modes
senses.titleCN: 横跨两个领域的：比喻用法
senses.definition: functioning in two different environments or modes, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻在两种不同环境或模式下运作
senses.example: She lived an amphibious life between the studio and the trading floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她在画室与交易所之间过着双栖生活。
senses.why: Any double life, literal or not, invites the amphibian image.
senses.whyCN: 任何「双重生活」，无论字面与否，都会引来两栖意象。

intro.en: Amphibious comes from Greek amphibios, living a double life, from amphi (both) plus bios (life).
intro.cn: amphibious 源自希腊语 amphibios「过双重生活的」，由 amphi（双向）加 bios（生命）构成。

items.en: Root *gweih-, to live, source of bios and biology.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *gweih-「生活」，是 bios 与 biology 的来源。

items.en: amphi, on both sides; bios, life; amphibios, leading a double life.
items.cn: 希腊语 amphi「两边」；bios「生命」；amphibios「双重生活」。

items.en: amphibius borrowed from Greek in natural history writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语在博物学著作中借入 amphibius。

items.en: English amphibious first described creatures living on land and in water.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 amphibious 先用于描述水陆两栖生物。

items.en: The word extended to plants, then to machines and military operations.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪该词扩展到植物，再到机械与军事行动。

items.en: Now standard in zoology, engineering, and military terminology.
items.cn: 如今是动物学、工程学与军事术语的标准用词。

note.en: Distinguish amphibious from its amphi- cousins and from words of double nature.
note.cn: 区分 amphibious 与其他 amphi- 前缀词，以及表示双重属性的词。

entries.definition: noun for a two-living creature or craft; amphibious is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「两栖动物/两栖飞机」；amphibious 是其形容词。

entries.definition: a round theater with seats on all sides; amphi- here means around, not double life.
entries.definitionCN: 环形剧场；amphi- 此处指「四周环绕」，与「双重生活」无关。

entries.definition: open to two readings; from ambigere, not from bios.
entries.definitionCN: 模棱两可的；源自拉丁语 ambigere，词根不同，勿与 amphibious 混。

entries.definition: living or growing in water only; half of the amphibious range.
entries.definitionCN: 水生的；只覆盖两栖范围的一半。

entries.definition: living on land only; the other half.
entries.definitionCN: 陆生的；两栖范围的另一半。

entries.definition: a mix of two kinds; broader double-nature idea.
entries.definitionCN: 混合的；泛指两种属性的结合。

normalIntro.en: Fix amphibious by hearing both lives inside it.
normalIntro.cn: 听出 amphibious 里的「双重生命」就能记牢。

normal.en: amphi (both) + bios (life) + -ous: living both ways.
normal.cn: amphi（双向）+ bios（生命）+ -ous：过双重生活。

normal.en: amphi family: amphibious (two lives), amphitheater (seats all around).
normal.cn: amphi 词族：amphibious（两栖）、amphitheater（环形剧场）。

normal.en: Anchor image: a frog, half swimmer, half jumper.
normal.cn: 锚定画面：青蛙，一半是泳者，一半是跳将。

normal.en: Military set phrase: amphibious landing ship.
normal.cn: 军事固定短语：amphibious landing ship（两栖登陆舰）。

normal.en: The noun amphibian doubles as both animal and aircraft.
normal.cn: 名词 amphibian 既指两栖动物也指两栖飞机。

abstract.en: See a truck splash into a river and keep driving on the riverbed.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车冲进河里，继续在河床上行驶。

abstract.en: A seal hauled out on the rocks, at home in both worlds.
abstract.cn: 海豹爬上礁石，在两个世界里都自在。

abstract.en: Bilingual professional by day, fisherman at dawn — amphibious schedule.
abstract.cn: 白天双语白领、清晨垂钓者——「两栖」日程。

examples.en: Salamanders are shy amphibious animals of the forest streams.
examples.cn: 蝾螈是林间溪流中羞怯的两栖动物。

examples.en: The navy tested a new amphibious transport dock.
examples.cn: 海军测试了一艘新型两栖船坞运输舰。

examples.en: Rescue teams used amphibious vehicles in the flooded town.
examples.cn: 救援队在被淹的城镇使用水陆两用车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安母比鹅死」——青蛙妈妈跟鹅比游泳，鹅输了（比鹅死），因为青蛙水陆两栖，水里赢了鹅。

root: 希腊语 amphi（两边、双向）+ bios（生命，源自印欧词根 *gweih-「生活」）→ amphibios（双重生活）→ 拉丁语 amphibius → 英语 amphibious（水陆两栖的）。同前缀词：amphitheater（环形剧场）、amphora（双耳瓶）。

sensesIntro.en: From the double life of frogs, amphibious spreads to plants, machines, armies, and anyone living in two worlds.
sensesIntro.cn: 从青蛙的双重生活出发，amphibious 扩展到植物、机械、军队乃至活在两个世界的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one creature owning two worlds
core.cn: 核心意象：一只生灵同时拥有两个世界

branches.en: Animals at home in water and on land
branches.cn: 水陆两栖的动物

branches.en: Plants rooted in both worlds
branches.cn: 水陆两生的植物

branches.en: Armies stepping from ship to shore
branches.cn: 由舰上岸的两栖作战

branches.en: Vehicles engineered for both terrains
branches.cn: 双地形设计的载具

branches.en: People or habits spanning two realms
branches.cn: 横跨两个领域的比喻用法

intro.en: Amphibious shows the Greek prefix amphi- doing its job of spanning two sides.
intro.cn: amphibious 展示了希腊前缀 amphi-「横跨两边」的构词功能。

latinIntro.en: The amphi- family marks symmetry and doubleness across English.
latinIntro.cn: amphi- 词族在英语中标记对称与双重。

definition_zh: 喧闹混乱的场面；疯人院
definition_en: a scene of wild uproar and confusion; historically, a madhouse
core_image: 股市崩盘时的大厅：人人喊叫，纸片乱飞
scene: 开市铃一响，大厅里人声鼎沸、一片混乱。 The trading floor became utter bedlam within seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 bedlam 是「喧闹混乱的场面」（第 1 个义项：极度嘈杂与混乱）；句意是交易大厅几秒内乱作一团。

senses.title: Wild uproar and confusion
senses.definition: a place or situation of extreme noise and disorder
senses.definitionCN: 极度嘈杂与混乱的地方或场面
senses.example: The trading floor became utter bedlam within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 交易大厅几秒内乱作一团。
senses.why: Visitors once flocked to gawk at the asylum's chaos, so the name spread to any uproar.
senses.whyCN: 昔日人们曾蜂拥围观疯人院的混乱，于是院名泛化为一切喧嚣。

senses.title: A madhouse
senses.definition: a hospital or asylum for the mentally ill, in historical use
senses.definitionCN: 收容精神病患的医院或院所（历史用法）
senses.example: In old London, Bedlam stood where the museum stands today.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧伦敦，伯利恒疯人院就坐落在今天博物馆的位置。
senses.why: The word is a worn-down form of Bethlehem, the asylum's name.
senses.whyCN: 该词是 Bethlehem（伯利恒，疯人院之名）的音讹缩略。

intro.en: Bedlam is London's Hospital of Bethlehem worn smooth by speech.
intro.cn: bedlam 是伦敦伯利恒医院之名在口语中磨损而成。

items.en: Bethlehem means house of bread.
items.cn: 希伯来语 Bethlehem 意为「粮屋」。

items.en: the London priory of St Mary of Bethlehem housed the insane by the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪起伦敦伯利恒圣母修道院收容精神病人。

items.en: the hospital's name was pronounced Bedlam in common speech.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪院名在日常口语中读作 Bedlam。

items.en: visiting the asylum became a public spectacle.
items.cn: 十七世纪参观疯人院成为公开的猎奇活动。

items.en: bedlam now means any uproarious scene, and the hospital is properly Bethlem Royal Hospital.
items.cn: 如今 bedlam 泛指喧闹场面；该医院现名 Bethlem Royal Hospital。

sensesIntro.en: One hospital's name became the word for chaos everywhere.

definition_zh: 信念体系；一套相互关联的信仰与看法；宗教教义体系；意识形态
definition_en: an organized set of beliefs that a person or a group holds and uses to explain the world
core_image: 屋架的柱、梁与斜撑互相扣住，抽掉其中一根，整片屋顶就塌下来
scene: 展柜里并排放着经卷、念珠和祭祀陶器，说明牌把它们归在同一套观念之下。 The exhibit shows how a belief system organizes ritual, law and daily habit.
sceneCN: 这里 belief system 指「一套彼此关联、共同支撑世界观的信念」（第 1 个义项：成体系的信念集合）；句意为展览说明这套信念体系如何组织仪式、律法与日常习惯。可辨识物件：经卷、念珠、陶器、说明牌。

pos.zh: 信念体系；成套的信仰与看法（可数，复数 belief systems）

collocations.zh: 占主导地位的信念体系

collocations.phrase: the belief system of a culture

derivatives.zh: 基础词 belief 作复合词前项，由「相信」这一状态偏移为「体系中的一条信念」
希腊 systema「组合起来的整体」进入英语，作复合词后项，偏移为「有组织的整体」
system + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 由「体系」偏移为「波及整个体系的」
system + -atic（形容词后缀）→ 偏移为「有步骤、成方法的」
systematic + -ize（动词后缀）→ 偏移为「把零散材料整理成体系」
systematize + -ation（动作名词后缀）→ 偏移为「体系化的过程」
believe + -er（施事后缀）→ 偏移为「在这套体系中信从的人」

senses.title: An organized set of beliefs
senses.definition: a set of beliefs that are linked together so that each supports the others
senses.definitionCN: 一组彼此连接、互相支撑的信念
senses.example: The exhibit shows how a belief system organizes ritual, law and daily habit.
senses.exampleCN: 展览展示了一套信念体系如何组织仪式、律法与日常习惯。
senses.why: system names a whole whose parts hold each other up, so a belief system is not a list of opinions but a structure.
senses.whyCN: system 指各部分互相撑持的整体，因此信念体系不是一张意见清单，而是一个结构。

senses.title: A religion's doctrinal whole
senses.definition: the complete body of doctrine, story and practice that a religion holds together
senses.definitionCN: 某一宗教把教义、故事与实践合在一起的整体
senses.example: Missionaries had to learn the whole belief system before preaching.
senses.exampleCN: 传教士必须先弄懂整套教义体系才能布道。
senses.why: religions are the clearest case of beliefs that must fit together, so the phrase is used most often for them.
senses.whyCN: 宗教是最典型的「信念必须彼此契合」的例子，因此这个说法最常用于宗教。

senses.title: A culture's shared worldview
senses.titleCN: 一个文化共享的世界观
senses.definition: the common assumptions a culture makes about what exists and what matters
senses.definitionCN: 一个文化对「存在什么、什么重要」的共同预设
senses.example: Rice farming shaped a belief system centred on water and cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻种植塑造了一套以水与合作为中心的信念体系。
senses.why: a culture's assumptions cluster the same way, so anthropologists borrowed the phrase for the whole cluster.
senses.whyCN: 一个文化的预设也以同样的方式聚成簇，人类学者便把这一说法借去指整个簇。

senses.title: A personal framework
senses.definition: an individual's settled set of assumptions used to interpret events
senses.definitionCN: 个人用来解释事件的一套稳定预设
senses.example: Trauma can shake a person's entire belief system.
senses.exampleCN: 创伤可能动摇一个人整套的信念框架。
senses.why: the phrase applies to one mind as easily as to a group, because coherence is needed at either scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法同样适用于单个头脑，因为无论规模大小都需要自洽。

senses.title: A political ideology
senses.definition: a connected set of political beliefs that justifies a programme of action
senses.definitionCN: 为一套行动纲领提供理由的、彼此关联的政治信念
senses.example: The party's belief system left little room for compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的意识形态几乎没有留下妥协的余地。
senses.why: ideologies are belief systems built for action, so the phrase often carries a critical edge in politics.
senses.whyCN: 意识形态是为行动而建的信念体系，因此这个说法在政治语境中常带批评意味。

senses.title: A philosophical system
senses.definition: a reasoned structure of principles that hangs together as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 由原理构成、整体自洽的论证结构
senses.example: His belief system rested on three unproved premises.
senses.exampleCN: 他的哲学体系建立在三个未加证明的前提上。
senses.why: philosophy builds exactly the kind of interlocking whole that the word system names.
senses.whyCN: 哲学所建的正是 system 一词所指的那种互相扣合的整体。

senses.title: A coping framework
senses.definition: the assumptions a person uses to make painful events bearable and meaningful
senses.definitionCN: 个人用来让痛苦事件变得可承受、有意义的预设
senses.example: Her belief system gave the illness a place she could live with.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信念框架给这场病安排了一个她能与之共处的位置。
senses.why: psychology found that people need a coherent frame to endure loss, and reused the phrase for that frame.
senses.whyCN: 心理学发现人需要一个自洽的框架才能承受失去，便把这个说法再次用于那个框架。

senses.title: An institutionalized creed
senses.definition: beliefs that an institution has fixed in texts, offices and routines
senses.definitionCN: 被机构固定进文本、职位与常规之中的信念
senses.example: The school's belief system survives in its entrance ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的信念体系在它的入学典礼中留存下来。
senses.why: once beliefs are written into offices and calendars, the system outlives the believers who hold it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦信念被写进职位与日程，这套体系就比持有它的个人活得更久。

intro.en: Belief system joins a native English noun for held truth to a Greek noun for an organized whole; the compound itself is a modern term of anthropology and psychology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: belief system 把指「所信之事」的英语本族名词，与指「有组织整体」的希腊名词组合起来；这个复合词本身是近代人类学与心理学的术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Belief came from the Germanic stock *ga-laubon 'to hold dear, approve', which developed the sense 'to hold as true'.
items.cn: belief 来自日耳曼词根 *ga-laubon「看重、认可」，由此发展出「当作真的」这一意思。

items.en: Greek systema meant 'an organized whole', generally thought to be built on syn- 'together' plus histanai 'to cause to stand'.
items.cn: 希腊 systema 意为「有组织的整体」，一般认为由 syn-「一起」加 histanai「使站立」构成。

items.en: Late Latin took systema as a Greek loanword, and from it came the learned vocabulary of system in the modern languages.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁把 systema 作为希腊借词吸收，近代诸语言的 system 学术词汇由此而来。

items.en: French système carried the word into general use, where it came to mean any set of parts working as a whole.
items.cn: 法语 système 把这个词带入一般用法，指任何共同运作的一套部分。

items.en: Belief system appears as a compound in nineteenth and twentieth century writing on religion, anthropology and psychology.
items.cn: belief system 作为复合词出现在十九与二十世纪关于宗教、人类学与心理学的著作中。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact compound is not recorded, and the pre-Greek origin of systema is unsettled, so any earlier form proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词的确切首见没有记录，systema 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，因此为它提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the compound from the single items and neighbouring set-words it is confused with; group two holds larger social and personal frames of reference.
note.cn: 第一组把这一复合词与单个信念及邻近的「成套」词分开；第二组是更大的社会与个人参照框架。

entries.definition: A single thing held as true; a belief system is the structure that holds many such items together.
entries.definitionCN: 单件被当作真的事；信念体系是把许多这样的条目撑在一起的结构。

entries.definition: A ranked set of moral preferences about right and wrong; it judges conduct, while a belief system explains what is.
entries.definitionCN: 关于对错的一套有排序的道德偏好；它评判行为，而信念体系说明「是什么」。

entries.definition: A person's overall picture of reality; it is close to belief system but stresses the picture rather than the linked propositions.
entries.definitionCN: 个人对现实的整体图景；与信念体系接近，但侧重图景本身，而非彼此连接的命题。

entries.definition: The beliefs of a religion set out in formal statements; it is the written core of a belief system, not the whole living system.
entries.definitionCN: 以正式条文列出的宗教信念；它是信念体系成文的核心，而不是整套活的体系。

entries.definition: A body of teaching handed down by an authority; it is what is taught, while a belief system is what is actually held.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威传下的一套教导；它指被教的内容，而信念体系指实际被持有的内容。

entries.definition: A system of ideas that justifies political action; it is a belief system recruited for power.
entries.definitionCN: 为政治行动提供理由的观念体系；可以说是被权力征用的信念体系。

entries.definition: An organized community, practice and doctrine; it includes a belief system but also buildings, offices and calendars.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的群体、实践与教义；它包含信念体系，也包含建筑、职位与日程。

entries.definition: A reasoned account of existence and knowledge; it values argument, where a belief system may rest on authority.
entries.definitionCN: 对存在与知识的论证性说明；它看重论证，而信念体系可能依靠权威。

entries.definition: A settled mental attitude that shapes how problems are met; it is looser and less codified than a belief system.
entries.definitionCN: 塑造应对问题方式的稳定心态；比信念体系更松散，也更少成文。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, its real set-phrases and its real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词两个真实的部分、它真实的固定说法与真实同族词。

normal.en: belief + system: held truths plus a structure that makes them hold each other up.
normal.cn: belief 加 system：被持有的真，加上一个使它们彼此撑持的结构。

normal.en: Greek syn- 'together' + histanai 'to stand' gives system: parts made to stand together.
normal.cn: 希腊 syn-「一起」加 histanai「站立」构成 system：被使之一同站住的部分。

normal.en: The family runs belief, believe, believer, system, systemic, systematic, systematize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 belief、believe、believer、system、systemic、systematic、systematize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: shared belief system, religious belief system, dominant belief system.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：共同信念体系、宗教信念体系、主导信念体系。

normal.en: Remove one supporting beam and the roof falls: that is what coherence means here.
normal.cn: 抽掉一根承重的梁，屋顶就塌：这就是此处「自洽」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a roof held up by beams that lean on one another rather than on the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一片屋顶由互相倚靠的梁撑起，而不是撑在地上。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring where every key opens a door that leads to the next key.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，每一把打开的门后都放着下一把。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence in which no word can be removed without the grammar collapsing.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话，去掉任何一个词，语法就整个垮掉。

examples.en: A belief system that cannot absorb contradiction eventually splits.
examples.cn: 无法容纳矛盾的信念体系最终会分裂。

examples.en: Fieldwork requires understanding a belief system from the inside.
examples.cn: 田野调查要求从内部理解一套信念体系。

examples.en: Two belief systems can share a practice and still disagree about why it matters.
examples.cn: 两套信念体系可以共享同一种做法，却对它的意义意见相反。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「belief（信念）+ system（系统）」——许多条信念按系统扣在一起 → 信念体系

root: belief（古英语「看重、相信」，日耳曼 *ga-laubon）+ system（希腊 systema「有组织的整体」，一般认为由 syn-「一起」+ histanai「使站立」构成）。复合词为近代人类学与心理学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one structure: separate beliefs are made to lean on one another, and the same structure is then found in a religion, a culture, one mind, a political programme, a philosophy, a coping frame and finally in written institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个结构展开：零散的信念被安排成互相倚靠，随后这同一结构依次出现在宗教、文化、单个头脑、政治纲领、哲学、应对框架，最后落在成文的制度里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame whose parts hold each other up, so that removing one brings the whole down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个各部分互相撑持的框架，抽掉一处，整体就塌。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE ITSELF: beliefs become a system only when each one supports the others.
branches.cn: 结构本身：只有当每条信念都支撑其他信念时，它们才成为体系。

branches.en: THE GREAT WHOLE: religion and philosophy are the two oldest examples of beliefs fitted into one coherent frame.
branches.cn: 宏大的整体：宗教与哲学是把信念装进一个自洽框架的最古老两个例子。

branches.en: FROM SHARED TO WRITTEN: a culture's assumptions become an institution's fixed texts and routines.
branches.cn: 从共享到成文：文化的预设变成机构固定的文本与常规。

branches.en: ONE MIND: the same frame is needed to interpret events and to bear what cannot be changed.
branches.cn: 单个头脑：解释事件与承受不可改变之事，需要的是同一个框架。

branches.en: BELIEFS RECRUITED FOR ACTION: an ideology is a system organized around a programme rather than around explanation.
branches.cn: 为行动征用的信念：意识形态是围绕纲领、而非围绕解释组织起来的体系。

intro.en: The compound can be read as two complete words, and each half brings its own family of suffixes and prefixes.
intro.cn: 这个复合词可按两个完整的词读出，每一半都带来自己的后缀与前缀词族。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a Latin trace: systema was a Greek noun borrowed into Late Latin, and it brought syn- and the root of histanai with it.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半部分留有拉丁痕迹：systema 是借入晚期拉丁的希腊名词，并随之带来 syn- 与 histanai 的词根。

items.example: The belief took root over generations.
items.exampleCN: 这条信念历经数代才扎下根。

items.example: The system failed at its weakest joint.
items.exampleCN: 这套体系在最弱的一处接合点失效了。

items.example: The prefix marks union rather than separation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记的是联合，而非分离。

items.example: The root supplies the standing in system.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了 system 中「站立」的意思。

items.example: The failure was systemic, not local.

definition_zh: 清淡的；乏味的；温和的；平淡无奇的
definition_en: lacking strong flavour, or lacking excitement and strong character
core_image: 一碗没放盐的白粥
scene: 食客尝了一口汤，默默地又撒了半勺盐。 The soup was too bland for my taste.
sceneCN: 这里 bland 是「清淡无味的」（第 1 个义项：食物缺少味道）；句意是这汤太淡，不合我的口味。

pos.zh: 清淡的；乏味的；温和的

derivatives.zh: bland 加 -ly，义为「温和地；乏味地」
bland 加 -ness，义为「平淡；温和无奇」
同源动词，义为「讨好；奉承」

senses.title: Lacking strong flavour
senses.definition: food that has little or no strong taste
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有浓烈味道的食物
senses.example: The soup was too bland for my taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤太淡，不合我的口味。
senses.why: Flavour is a kind of heat or force, and bland names its absence.
senses.whyCN: 味道本是一种力道，bland 标记的正是力道的缺席。

senses.title: Gentle and soothing, of remedies
senses.definition: of medicine or soap, mild and not irritating
senses.definitionCN: 药物或清洁用品性质温和、不刺激
senses.example: Wash the rash with bland soap and water.
senses.exampleCN: 用温和的肥皂和清水清洗皮疹。
senses.why: What carries no force cannot sting, so mild things keep the bland name.
senses.whyCN: 不带力道之物不会刺痛，温和之物因而沿用此名。

senses.title: Showing no strong emotion
senses.definition: of a face or manner, calm and showing no strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 面容或态度平和、不见强烈情绪
senses.example: He gave a bland smile and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他淡淡一笑，换了个话题。
senses.why: A face without expression is like food without salt: nothing registers.
senses.whyCN: 没有表情的脸如无盐的菜：什么都尝不出来。

senses.title: Dull and uninteresting
senses.definition: so lacking in interest or excitement that it bores
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味或刺激到令人厌倦
senses.example: The film's bland plot forgot to thrill anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 影片平淡的情节没能让任何人兴奋。
senses.why: Excitement is flavour for the mind, and its absence earns the same word.
senses.whyCN: 刺激之于头脑如味道之于舌头，缺席时共用其名。

senses.title: Deliberately neutral in speech
senses.definition: of statements, carefully neutral so as to offend no one
senses.definitionCN: 言辞刻意中性，避免冒犯任何人
senses.example: The statement was bland enough to mean nothing at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这份声明四平八稳到毫无实义。
senses.why: Removing all edge from words leaves only blandness, like watered soup.
senses.whyCN: 把言辞的锋芒全部去掉，只剩清汤寡水般的平淡。

senses.title: Lacking distinctive character
senses.definition: of places or designs, unremarkable and without identity
senses.definitionCN: 场所或设计毫无辨识度、千篇一律
senses.example: Airport hotels everywhere look bland and identical.
senses.exampleCN: 各地的机场酒店看上去千篇一律、毫无特色。
senses.why: Character is the spice of a place; strip it and the place reads as bland.
senses.whyCN: 特色是地方之香料，剥去之后便只剩平淡。

senses.title: Smooth-mannered to the point of insincerity
senses.definition: polite and smooth in a way that seems hollow
senses.definitionCN: 客气圆滑却显得空洞无诚
senses.example: The salesman's bland charm wore thin fast.
senses.exampleCN: 推销员那副圆滑的殷勤很快就让人腻烦。
senses.why: Charm without conviction tastes as empty as a spiceless dish.
senses.whyCN: 没有诚意的魅力，如没有香料的菜一样空乏。

senses.title: Of weather or light, mild and unvarying
senses.definition: of climate or light, mild and without sharp change
senses.definitionCN: 气候或光线温和且少有剧烈变化
senses.example: The coast enjoys a bland climate all year.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸全年气候温和宜人。
senses.why: Weather without sting or storm keeps the mild, bland name.
senses.whyCN: 不冷不烈、无风无暴的天气沿用「温和」之名。

intro.en: Bland comes from Latin blandus, soft-tongued and flattering.
intro.cn: bland 来自拉丁语 blandus，本义「言辞温柔的、谄媚的」。

items.en: possibly a nasalized form of a root meaning to move slowly or gently; origin uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为出自表示「缓慢、轻柔」之意的词根的鼻化形式，来源不确定。

items.en: blandus meant caressing, flattering, mild in speech.
items.cn: 拉丁语 blandus 意为「抚慰的、谄媚的、言辞温和的」。

items.en: blando kept the soft, gentle sense.
items.cn: 意大利语 blando 保留「柔软、温和」之义。

items.en: blando likewise means soft.
items.cn: 西班牙语 blando 同样意为「柔软的」。

items.en: English took blandus for smooth and flattering speech, then for mildness of every kind.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪借入，先指言辞圆滑讨巧，后扩指各类温和无味。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bland- root; the near-meaning group gathers mild, flavourless words.

abstract.en: Picture a grey corridor with no picture on any wall.

definition_zh: 超过；胜过；超越
definition_en: to go beyond a limit, record or standard, or to be better than someone or something else
core_image: 终点线旁的数字牌被人越过，上一年的纪录还挂在牌上，新数字已经翻过去
scene: 年底还没到，出口额就已经比去年全年更多。 Exports are expected to surpass last year's total.
sceneCN: 这里指在数量上超过原有水平（第 1 个义项：数量或数字超过）；句意为出口额预计会超过去年全年总量。图中可辨识物件：终点线、翻过去的数字牌、旧纪录。

pos.zh: 超过；胜过；超越

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「非凡的；超越的」
由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「无可匹敌的」
由该动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可超越的」（少用）
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已被超越的」

senses.title: To exceed a number
senses.definition: to be greater than a stated figure, total or level
senses.definitionCN: 大于某个给定的数字、总量或水平
senses.example: Sales surpassed ten million units this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年销量超过了一千万台。
senses.why: The Old French verb meant to pass over, and a figure is something you can pass.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词意为「越过」，而数字正是可以越过去的东西。

senses.title: To outperform a rival
senses.definition: to do better than a competitor in a contest or market
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛或市场中表现得比对手更好
senses.example: The small team surpassed three larger firms in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小团队在测试中胜过了三家更大的公司。
senses.why: A race is the original scene: one runner passes another and is now ahead.
senses.whyCN: 赛跑是最初的场景：一名跑者越过另一名，就跑到前面了。

senses.title: To exceed expectations
senses.definition: to be better or larger than people had predicted
senses.definitionCN: 比人们此前预料的更好或更大
senses.example: The response to the appeal surpassed every forecast.
senses.exampleCN: 这次呼吁得到的响应超出了所有预测。
senses.why: Expectations set a line in advance, and surpassing is crossing that line.
senses.whyCN: 预期提前画了一条线，超过就是越过那条线。

senses.title: To break a record
senses.definition: to go beyond the best result previously achieved
senses.definitionCN: 超过此前取得的最好成绩
senses.example: She surpassed the national record by two hundredths of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 她以百分之二秒打破了全国纪录。
senses.why: A record is the highest mark on the board, and the verb names the moment it falls.
senses.whyCN: 纪录是板上最高的刻度，这个词命名它被刷下的那一刻。

senses.title: To go beyond a limit of ability
senses.definition: to be more than a person or system can reach or handle
senses.definitionCN: 超过人或系统所能达到或处理的范围
senses.example: The noise surpassed the level the equipment could measure.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声超过了设备能够测量的水平。
senses.why: A limit is a wall, and surpassing passes over it rather than around it.
senses.whyCN: 极限是一堵墙，而超过是从上方越过去，不是绕过去。

senses.title: To be superior in quality
senses.definition: to be of better quality than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类的另一事物之上
senses.example: The finish surpassed every sample we had tested.
senses.exampleCN: 这层表面处理胜过我们测过的所有样品。
senses.why: Quality can be ranked, and the higher rank simply sits beyond the lower one.
senses.whyCN: 质量可以排位，较高的位次就落在较低位次之外。

senses.title: To outdo one's earlier self
senses.definition: to do better than one's own previous performance
senses.definitionCN: 比自己以往的表现做得更好
senses.example: He surpassed his own best time in the final heat.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一组超过了自己的最好成绩。
senses.why: The rival can be oneself, which is why the word often appears with the reflexive form.
senses.whyCN: 对手可以就是自己，所以这个词常与反身形式同现。

senses.title: To go over a set ceiling
senses.definition: to rise above a ceiling set by policy, safety or design
senses.definitionCN: 上升到由政策、安全或设计设定的上限之上
senses.example: Demand surpassed the capacity of the old substation.
senses.exampleCN: 需求超过了旧变电站的容量。
senses.why: Every design has a ceiling, and surpassing it is the point where a plan stops being safe.
senses.whyCN: 每个设计都有上限，超过它就是方案不再安全的那个点。

intro.en: Surpass comes from Old French surpasser, to go beyond, from sur-, over, and passer, to pass, which goes back to Latin passus, a step. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 surpasser「越过」，由 sur-「在上、超过」与 passer「经过」构成，而 passer 可追溯到拉丁语 passus「一步」；英语十六世纪引入。

items.en: Passus meant a step or a pace, and it is the source of pass, passage and surpass alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为一步或一步的距离，是 pass、passage、surpass 共同的来源。

items.en: The prefix behind sur- meant above or over, and it survives in super, supreme and surface.
items.cn: sur- 背后的前缀意为在上、越过，仍见于 super、supreme、surface。

items.en: The French verb meant to go beyond or to exceed, and it was used of limits, rivals and expectations.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为越过、超过，用于界限、对手与预期。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪采用这个动词，确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十六世纪」。

items.en: Surplus, survive and surrender share the same over- prefix with different roots behind it.
items.cn: surplus、survive、surrender 共享同一「在上」前缀，背后的词根各不相同。

items.en: Sport gave the verb its fixed objects record and rival, which keep the race image alive.
items.cn: 体育给这个动词添了纪录与对手这两个固定宾语，让赛跑画面延续至今。

note.en: The first group shares the pass root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of excelling.
note.cn: 第一组与「surpass」共享 pass 词根或只是形近；第二组是与「胜过」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning exceptional, literally going beyond others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指非凡的，字面是「越过他人」。

entries.definition: Not exceeded by anything, the negative adjective of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指无人超过的，是这个动词的否定形容词。

entries.definition: Capable of being exceeded, a rare but regular form.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被超过的，少用但构词规则。

entries.definition: To go by or beyond, the base verb inside surpass.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过或越过，是这个词内部的基础动词。

entries.definition: An amount over what is needed; the prefix matches but the root is to be more.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出所需的数量；前缀相同，词根是「更多」。

entries.definition: The top layer, from sur- and face; the prefix matches, the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指表层，由「在上」前缀与「面」构成；前缀相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: To go beyond a number or a limit, the neutral technical verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出数量或限度，是中性技术说法。

entries.definition: To do better than someone in the same activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一活动中做得比某人更好。

entries.definition: To perform better than a rival, common in business.
entries.definitionCN: 指表现优于对手，商务常用。

entries.definition: To defeat or do better than, in plain speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指击败或胜过，口语说法。

entries.definition: To go beyond a category or limit altogether, often in a philosophical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体上超越某个范畴或限度，常带哲学意味。

entries.definition: To be higher than a previous figure, used of charts and lists.
entries.definitionCN: 指高于先前数字，多用于榜单。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the step root, the over prefix, and the sporting phrases that keep the race image alive.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「一步」词根、「在上」前缀，以及让赛跑画面延续的体育搭配。

normal.en: Passus is a step, and surpass is to step over the line that was there.
normal.cn: passus 是「一步」，而这个词就是跨过原先那条线。

normal.en: Sur- means over, the same prefix seen in surplus and surface.
normal.cn: sur- 意为「在上」，与 surplus、surface 同一前缀。

normal.en: Athletes surpass a record; firms surpass expectations and rivals.
normal.cn: 运动员打破纪录，企业超出预期、胜过对手。

normal.en: Unsurpassed is the negative adjective: nobody has gone past it.
normal.cn: 「无可匹敌的」是否定形容词：没人越过去过。

normal.en: Unlike transcend, surpass is measurable: a number, a time or a rank moves past another.
normal.cn: 与 transcend 不同，surpass 是可测量的：数字、时间或名次越到另一个前面。

abstract.en: To surpass is to make yesterday's ceiling today's floor.
abstract.cn: 超越，就是把昨天的天花板变成今天的地板。

abstract.en: Every record is only a place where someone stopped being measured.
abstract.cn: 每一项纪录都只是有人停止被测量的那个位置。

abstract.en: Transcend changes the scale; surpass merely moves along it, and knowing which one you need is the real skill.
abstract.cn: 超越范畴是换一把尺，胜过只是在同一把尺上往前挪，分得清两者才是真本事。

examples.en: Demand for the service surpassed all earlier estimates.
examples.cn: 这项服务的需求超出了此前所有估计。

examples.en: Her second novel surpassed the first in every review.
examples.cn: 她的第二部小说在每一篇评论中都胜过了第一部。

examples.en: The river surpassed its danger level after two days of rain.
examples.cn: 两天降雨之后，这条河超过了警戒水位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑟帕斯」——终点牌被翻过去，旧纪录留在上面：超过、胜过

root: 拉丁语 passus「一步」→ 古法语 surpasser「越过」（sur-「在上」+ passer「经过」）；英语十六世纪引入。与 transcend 不同，本词强调可测量的越线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all cross a line: a number, a rival, a forecast, a record, a limit, a quality, one's own best and a ceiling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在越过一条线：数字、对手、预测、纪录、极限、质量、自己的最好成绩与上限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner crosses the line and the board turns past last year's figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑者冲过终点线，数字牌翻过去年的数字。

branches.en: THE FIGURE IS PASSED: a total or a ceiling is left below the new reading.
branches.cn: 数字被越过：总量或上限被留在新读数之下。

branches.en: THE RIVAL IS BEHIND: a competitor or a sample now ranks lower.
branches.cn: 对手落到后面：竞争者或样品的名次更低。

branches.en: THE FORECAST IS BEATEN: what people expected turns out to be too small.
branches.cn: 预测被打破：人们预想的原来偏小。

branches.en: THE MARK FALLS: a record or one's own previous best is replaced.
branches.cn: 刻度被刷下：纪录或自己从前的最好成绩被取代。

branches.en: THE ABILITY IS OUTRUN: a limit of reach, handling or understanding is passed.
branches.cn: 能力被跑过：触及、处理或理解的极限被越过。

intro.en: Surpass joins an over-prefix to a verb of stepping, and both pieces are Latin in origin though the compound is French.
intro.cn: 这个词把「在上」的前缀接到表示「迈步」的动词上，两部分都源自拉丁语，但复合发生在法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies passus and super; the French compound surpasser then supplied English, and every piece is well recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 passus 与 super；法语复合词 surpasser 再提供英语，每个部件都有清楚记录。

items.example: The noun is the source of pass and surpass.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 pass 与 surpass 的来源。

items.example: The French verb supplied the moving half.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词提供「移动」的那一半。

items.example: It marks the line being crossed.
items.exampleCN: 它标出被越过的那条线。

items.example: The Latin form behind the French prefix.
items.exampleCN: 法语前缀背后的拉丁形式。

items.example: The compound entered English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词几乎原样进入英语。

items.meaning: in the course of, or to a high degree

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「非凡的；超越的」
由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「无可匹敌的」
由该动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可超越的」（少用）
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已被超越的」

definition_zh: 艺术技巧；艺术性；精湛技艺
definition_en: great skill and creativity in an art or craft
core_image: 指尖在琴键上流出的灵光
scene: 老工匠打磨着琴身，木纹在灯下泛着琥珀光。 Visitors admired the artistry of the carved doorway.
sceneCN: 这里 artistry 是「精湛技艺」（第 1 个义项：艺术性的高超技巧）；句意是来访者赞叹雕花门廊的精美工艺。

pos.zh: 艺术技巧；艺术造诣
艺术性；巧夺天工的品质

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「艺术家」，artistry 由其加后缀 -ry 构成
art 加 -istic，义为「艺术的；有美感的」
同源词（拉丁 ars），义为「工匠」，与 artist 相对
词源基础，义为「艺术；技艺」

senses.title: Great artistic skill
senses.definition: exceptional ability and creative skill in performing or making
senses.definitionCN: 表演或创作中超凡的能力与创造性技巧
senses.example: The pianist played with effortless artistry.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家的演奏挥洒自如、技艺精湛。
senses.why: The suffix -ry names the quality or practice of the artist.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ry 表示「艺术家之特质或实践」。

senses.title: Artistic quality in a work
senses.definition: the degree to which a work shows beauty, imagination and craft
senses.definitionCN: 作品体现美感、想象与匠心的程度
senses.example: The film's artistry lies in its silent long shots.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的艺术性在于其无声的长镜头。
senses.why: The quality of the maker transfers to the made object.
senses.whyCN: 制作者的气质转移到作品之上。

intro.en: Artistry is artist plus the noun suffix -ry, formed within English in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: artistry 由 artist 加名词后缀 -ry 构成，19 世纪在英语内部生成。

items.en: Root *h2er- (to fit together) is reconstructed behind Latin ars.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h2er-（接合）位于拉丁语 ars 之下（重构形式）。

items.en: Ars meant skill, craft, method, the trained way of doing anything well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ars 意为技艺、方法，指把任何事做好的训练之道。

items.en: Old French art broadened the word toward fine art and learned skill.
items.cn: 古法语 art 使词义向美术与学问之技扩展。

items.en: Artistry formed on the model of artistry-like nouns in -ry, first recorded about 1837.
items.cn: artistry 仿 -ry 系名词构成，约 1837 年首见记载。

items.en: It now praises creative skill wherever it appears, from kitchens to code.
items.cn: 如今它赞美一切创造性技艺，从厨房到代码。

note.en: Artistry names the quality; artist the person; artistic the style.
note.cn: artistry 指品质，artist 指人，artistic 指风格。

entries.definition: a skilled manual craftsman
entries.definitionCN: 工匠，与 artistry 同出拉丁 ars 但指手艺人

entries.definition: a person who creates art
entries.definitionCN: 艺术家，artistry 的基础词

entries.definition: relating to art; showing taste
entries.definitionCN: 艺术的，artistry 的同根形容词

entries.definition: skill in a particular handcraft
entries.definitionCN: 手艺、工艺，与 artistry 义近而更重手上功夫

entries.definition: delicate skill and subtlety in handling
entries.definitionCN: 细腻精妙的技巧，与 artistry 义近

entries.definition: complete command of a skill
entries.definitionCN: 精通、驾驭自如，与 artistry 义近而泛指技艺

normalIntro.en: Build the word visibly: artist + ry = the artist's quality.
normalIntro.cn: 直观构词：artist + ry ＝ 艺术家之特质。

normal.en: artist + -ry = artistry, the quality of being artistic.
normal.cn: artist + -ry ＝ artistry，即艺术造诣。

normal.en: -ry builds quality nouns: bravery, robbery, artistry.
normal.cn: -ry 构成性质名词：bravery、robbery、artistry。

normal.en: Sheer artistry praises effortless perfection.
normal.cn: sheer artistry 赞叹浑然天成的完美。

normal.en: Compare artisan (craftsman) with artist (creator).
normal.cn: 对比 artisan（工匠）与 artist（创作者）。

normal.en: Adjective is artistic, not artistry-like.
normal.cn: 形容词是 artistic。

abstract.en: Watch a brush lift at exactly the right moment.
abstract.cn: 看画笔在最恰当的一瞬提起。

abstract.en: Hear a voice bend a single note into something new.
abstract.cn: 听一个音符在嗓音中被折出新的形状。

abstract.en: See wood shavings curling from a carver's blade like ribbons.
abstract.cn: 想象雕刀下木屑如缎带般卷起。

examples.en: The pastry chef's artistry drew crowds at the expo.
examples.cn: 糕点师的精湛手艺在博览会上吸引了大批观众。

examples.en: Critics praised the novel's narrative artistry.
examples.cn: 评论家盛赞这部小说的叙事艺术。

examples.en: There is real artistry in the way he codes.
examples.cn: 他写代码的方式颇具匠心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提·斯嘴」——阿提吹糖人全凭一张灵巧的嘴和手，糖丝在他嘴边转折如画，观者惊叹这「阿提斯」的艺术技巧。

root: 拉丁语 ars（技艺）→ 古法语 art → 英语 artist → artist + -ry（性质名词后缀）→ artistry；-ry 同族词有 bravery、jewelry。

sensesIntro.en: From the artist's exceptional skill to the artistic quality of a work.
sensesIntro.cn: 由艺术家的超凡技艺延伸到作品呈现的艺术性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: inspiration flowing from trained fingertips
core.cn: 核心意象：从训练有素的指尖流出的灵光

branches.en: the performer's command of craft
branches.cn: 表演者对技艺的驾驭

branches.en: beauty embodied in the work
branches.cn: 作品中的具象之美

branches.en: creative flair beyond technique
branches.cn: 超越技术的创造力

branches.en: the viewer's startled praise
branches.cn: 观者惊叹的赞辞

branches.en: artistry as measure of a work
branches.cn: 作为作品尺度的艺术性

intro.en: The suffix -ry turns nouns of person into nouns of quality or place.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ry 把指人名词变成性质或场所名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars traveled through French art into the whole art family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ars 经法语 art 延伸出整个 art 词族。

definition_zh: n. 网络空间；虚拟世界；网络领域
definition_en: the notional environment of computer networks where data, messages and virtual worlds exist
core_image: 一片没有地面的蓝色旷野，无数光点在其中连成路径
scene: 他把整份档案搬进了网络空间。 He moved the whole archive into cyberspace.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cyberspace 指网络构成的虚拟世界；句意是他把整份档案搬到网上。

pos.zh: 网络空间；虚拟世界；网络领域

senses.title: Virtual world
senses.definition: the imagined space formed by connected computers and their data
senses.definitionCN: 由互联计算机及其数据构成的想象空间
senses.example: Millions of people work in cyberspace every day.
senses.exampleCN: 每天有数百万人在网络空间里工作。
senses.why: A blue plain with no ground, only paths of light.
senses.whyCN: 一片没有地面的蓝色旷野，只有光的路径。

senses.title: Security domain
senses.definition: cyberspace treated as a field of law, defence and attack
senses.definitionCN: 被当作法律、防务与攻击领域的网络空间
senses.example: The treaty covers cyberspace as well as land and sea.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把网络空间与陆地、海洋一并涵盖。
senses.why: A map with a fifth colour for the network.
senses.whyCN: 一张为网络多添一种颜色的地图。

intro.en: Cyberspace was coined by William Gibson in 1982, from cybernetics plus space.
intro.cn: cyberspace 由威廉·吉布森于一九八二年创造，取自 cybernetics 加 space。

items.en: Kybernetes meant the steersman of a ship.
items.cn: kybernetes 意为船上的舵手。

items.en: Wiener named the science of control cybernetics.
items.cn: 一九四八年维纳把控制的科学命名为控制论。

items.en: Gibson coined cyberspace in a short story.
items.cn: 一九八二年吉布森在一篇短篇小说里创造了 cyberspace。

items.en: Neuromancer made cyberspace a shared hallucination.
items.cn: 一九八四年《神经漫游者》把 cyberspace 写成一场共享的幻觉。

items.en: Cyberspace became the everyday word for the online world.
items.cn: 二十世纪九十年代 cyberspace 成为网络世界的日常用语。

items.en: Armies and laws now treat cyberspace as a domain.
items.cn: 二十一世纪军队与法律把网络空间当作一个领域。

note.en: The look-alike group shares cyber- or -space; the near-meaning group names the connected world itself.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cyber- 或 -space；近义组指那个互联世界本身。

entries.definition: Relating to computers and networks.
entries.definitionCN: 网络的。

entries.definition: The science of control and communication.
entries.definitionCN: 控制论。

entries.definition: A being made of flesh and machine parts.
entries.definitionCN: 半机械人。

entries.definition: The part of the sky above a country.
entries.definitionCN: 领空。

entries.definition: The worldwide system of linked networks.
entries.definitionCN: 互联网。

entries.definition: The pages reachable through the internet.
entries.definitionCN: 万维网。

entries.definition: A set of connected computers or people.
entries.definitionCN: 网络。

entries.definition: A persistent shared virtual environment.
entries.definitionCN: 元宇宙。

normalIntro.en: Cyber means steer and space means room: a room you steer through.
normalIntro.cn: cyber 意为掌舵，space 意为空间：一个由你掌舵穿行的空间。

normal.en: A kybernetes steered a ship.
normal.cn: kybernetes 是掌舵的人。

normal.en: Cybernetics studies steering and control.
normal.cn: 控制论研究掌舵与控制。

normal.en: Cyber- carries that steering sense into computers.
normal.cn: cyber- 把掌舵的意思带进计算机。

normal.en: Space is the room where something happens.
normal.cn: space 是事情发生的场所。

normal.en: Cyberspace is the room you steer through online.
normal.cn: cyberspace 就是你在网上掌舵穿行的场所。

abstract.en: A blue plain with no ground.
abstract.cn: 一片没有地面的蓝色旷野。

abstract.en: A map with a fifth colour for the network.
abstract.cn: 一张为网络多添一种颜色的地图。

abstract.en: A shared hallucination of light and data.
abstract.cn: 一场由光与数据构成的共享幻觉。

examples.en: Rumours spread fast in cyberspace.
examples.cn: 谣言在网络空间里传得很快。

examples.en: The bank spent millions on cyberspace security.
examples.cn: 这家银行在网络空间安全上花了数百万。

examples.en: Her whole shop exists only in cyberspace.
examples.cn: 她的整间店铺只存在于网络空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: cyber（赛博＝掌舵）+ space（空间）＝一片靠你掌舵穿行的电子旷野。

root: 希腊 kybernetes（舵手）→ cybernetics（控制论）→ 吉布森造词 cyberspace

sensesIntro.en: From a steering metaphor to a fifth domain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个掌舵的比喻到第五个领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a groundless blue plain crossed by paths of light
core.cn: 核心意象：一片没有地面、被光路穿过的蓝色旷野

branches.en: A blue plain with no ground.
branches.cn: 一片没有地面的蓝色旷野。

branches.en: A map with a fifth colour for the network.
branches.cn: 一张为网络多添一种颜色的地图。

branches.en: A place you steer through and defend.
branches.cn: 一个既由你掌舵穿行、又需要防守的地方。

branches.en: A shared hallucination of light and data.
branches.cn: 一场由光与数据构成的共享幻觉。

branches.en: A border drawn around servers.
branches.cn: 一条围着服务器划出的边界。

intro.en: Cyberspace joins cyber-, from the Greek steersman, with space-.
intro.cn: cyberspace 由源自希腊语舵手的 cyber- 与 space- 拼合。

latinIntro.en: Greek kybernetes means steersman and Latin spatium means room or space.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kybernetes 意为舵手，拉丁语 spatium 意为场所或空间。
